10 South Colonnade, Canary Wharf, London, E14 4PU

About the job

Job summary

We are currently looking for a Service Delivery Manager to join our Innovative Devices within the Innovation & Compliance group.

This is a full-time opportunity, on a fixed term contract basis until 31 March 2029. Internal move, temporary promotion, loan will be considered.
The role will be based in 10 South Colonnade, Canary Wharf London, E14 4PU. Please be aware that this role can only be worked in the UK and not overseas.

Government departments and agencies are working towards implementing a minimum 60% attendance in office sites.

We are currently implementing a flexible, hybrid way of working, with a minimum of 8 days per month working on site to enable the collaboration and contact with partners and stakeholders needed to deliver MHRA business. Attendance on site is driven by business needs so depending on the nature of the role, this can flex up to 12 days a month, with the remainder of time worked either remotely or in the office. Some roles will need to be on site more regularly. Remote working is potentially available for some specific roles. Please discuss this with the recruiting manager before accepting an appointment.

Who are we?

The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency enhance and improve the health of millions of people every day through the effective regulation of medicines and medical devices, underpinned by science and research.

Innovation and Compliance (I&C) group delivers public health impact, world-leading research innovation, and a unique proposition via an ambitious Science Strategy which balances innovation against sustainability and affordability. It is divided into four sub-groups: Innovation Accelerator and Regulatory Science, Clinical Investigations and Trials, Standards and Compliance and Innovative Devices.

Job description

Role Purpose

The Early Access Service offers an exciting opportunity to be at the forefront of medical device innovation to address unmet patient need in the UK. The Early Access service was developed jointly the Medical Research Council and the MHRA, for innovative medical technologies, including diagnostics around early diagnosis of dementia, that meet a critical need in the health and care system. The aim of the service is to improve patient access to innovative technologies by providing developers with joined up support and advice from across the UK.

The role is the central coordinating interface between those defining requirements and the specialist teams undertaking technical and clinical assessment. The role ensures that inputs into the Early Access service are translated into coherent, timely and high quality technical and clinical assessments. The role holder will be responsible for shaping assessment requests, coordinating delivery across technical and clinical assessors, tracking progress against agreed plans, and providing clear, reliable updates to leadership and stakeholders. The role holder will also lead and work in collaboration with digital technology partners to develop a platform for an end-to-end Early Access Service, with view to scale up for future programs within Innovative Devices. This is an opportunity to modernise processes, improve data use, increase automation, improve reporting and support risk-proportionate decision-making in medical device assessments within MHRA and supporting the NHS 10-year plan and the Life Sciences Sector Plan.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead the development and implementation of processes, including the design and development of any technology platforms that may be required, for the Early Access Service.
  • Design and develop internal instructions for technical and clinical assessors based on requirements from policy and legislation.
  • Lead the end-to-end management of application submissions for the Early Access program, establishing proportionate governance, quality controls and clear service standards to ensure applications are handled consistently, transparently and in line with relevant policy, legislative and operational requirements. This may include:
    • Oversee validation and triage of applications, applying sound regulatory judgement to confirm eligibility, completeness and readiness for assessment; resolve complex or ambiguous issues, identify risks and dependencies, and ensure proportionate escalation and a clear audit trail for decisions.
    • Provide authoritative, risk-based regulatory advice and guidance to external stakeholders on the application process, translating complex requirements into clear and practical expectations, managing challenging enquiries, and influencing applicants to submit high-quality evidence that supports timely and robust assessment.
  • Manage the assessment process for the Early Access program, ensuring that assessments are conducted consistently, within deadlines and to the highest standards. This may include:
    • Ensure performance management arrangements of technical and clinical teams, clarify what’s needed, plan the tasks, and make sure work follows regulations and the Early Access service model.
    • Track progress of assessments, spot any risks or delays early, provide regular progress updates and analysis to senior managementand, and help decide priorities if there are too many tasks at once.
  • Lead on ongoing process improvement, data management, and automation within the MHRA, contributing to the Agency’s reputation as a leader in clinical research regulation.
  • Foster inclusive and collaborative working across operational, technical, clinical, policy and digital teams; resolve complex or competing priorities; and use feedback, performance information and lessons learned to improve efficiency, consistency and effectiveness across all operational areas.
  • Advise more senior managers on casework, policy and legislative development to ensure timely delivery of other cross-agency tasks and activities

The job description is not intended to be exhaustive and it is likely that responsibilities and outcomes may be altered from time to time in the light of changing circumstances and after consultation with the postholder.

Person specification

Essential Criteria:

• Experience working in a regulated, policy-led or operational environment.

• Experience in technical, scientific, or clinical assessment of medical devices or medicines.

• Experience leading the delivery of a service, programme, or coordinated workstream.

• Experience tracking work progress and providing clear updates to colleagues or stakeholders.

  • Minimum of bachelor’s degree in a medicine, science, engineering fields of study or equivalent experience developed through previous roles.
  • Excellent IT skills with proven ability to extract, analyse, interpret and present data. Confidence using digital tools (e.g. trackers, shared documents) to support service delivery, document and report progress, risks, issues clearly and accurately.
  • Experience in digital platform development and automation tools

title: Senior AI Product Manager
description:

We're a San Francisco & Montreal based applied AI startup that's building the future of work in the banking industry. We are tackling a $100 billion/yr problem, doubling every quarter and pushing the boundaries of what’s possible with multi-turn AI agentic systems.

Our goal is to tackle the type of automation problems that require long-context reasoning, tool orchestration across legacy systems, and strict compliance loops: the ones without known answers.

  • 5+ years of experience in implementation, product management, consulting, or enterprise onboarding—ideally with AI products in the banking/credit union industry.

  • Domain experience in an American bank or credit union

  • Expertise in workflow mapping, use case identification, and translating needs into product specs

  • Effective communication skills —experience and comfort in engaging with senior executives and leaders at financial institutions.

  • Growth mindset and curiosity - Have a growth mindset, drive initiatives, and a strong desire to help customers succeed.

Why Join Saris?

title: Engineering Shift Technician
description:
embecta is a global medical device company with a 100-year legacy in insulin delivery and diabetes care. Driven by innovation, purpose, and a commitment to improving lives, we are expanding our portfolio of solutions to serve even more patients, healthcare providers, and communities around the world.


We are seeking X 3 experienced Engineering Technicians to join our high performing manufacturing team in Dun Laoghaire.

Working within a modern, highly automated manufacturing environment, you will play a key role in maintaining, troubleshooting, and continuously improving production equipment to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operations.

Reporting to the Shift Process Engineer, you will be responsible for supporting plant performance through preventative maintenance, equipment optimisation, fault diagnosis, and continuous improvement initiatives.

What You'll Do

  • Install, maintain, modify, and repair a wide range of manufacturing and production equipment.
  • Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, and automation related equipment issues to minimise production downtime.
  • Perform preventative and corrective maintenance activities to the highest engineering standards.
  • Support continuous improvement projects focused on improving equipment reliability, efficiency, output, and product quality.
  • Participate in equipment validation activities, including commissioning, acceptance testing, debugging, and qualification of new and existing equipment.
  • Analyse equipment-related quality issues, customer complaints, and production defects, identifying and implementing corrective actions.
  • Collaborate with equipment suppliers, contractors, and external service providers as required.
  • Support the training and development of technicians, apprentices, and new team members.
  • Maintain accurate maintenance records, reports, and documentation using SAP and other business systems.
  • Promote and maintain the highest standards of safety, quality, and housekeeping across the manufacturing environment.
  • Participate in cross-functional teams and company-wide continuous improvement initiatives.

About You

You are a hands-on engineering professional who enjoys solving technical problems, improving equipment performance, and working in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Essential Qualifications & Experience

  • National Craft Certificate, Engineering Technician Qualification, or relevant third-level qualification in Mechanical, Electrical, Electronic, Mechatronic Engineering.
  • Experience working in a high-volume manufacturing, pharmaceutical, medical device, food, or regulated production environment.
  • Strong troubleshooting and fault-finding skills across mechanical and electrical systems.
  • Experience supporting automated production equipment and manufacturing processes.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capability with a structured approach to root cause investigation.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  • Good computer literacy and experience using maintenance management systems or SAP.

Desirable Experience

  • Experience in a regulated manufacturing environment (Medical Device, Pharmaceutical, or Life Sciences).
  • Knowledge of continuous improvement methodologies such as Lean Manufacturing, TPM, Six Sigma, or Kaizen.
  • Experience supporting equipment validation and qualification activities.

Shift Pattern

This position operates on a 24/7 manufacturing schedule and follows a 4-cycle shift pattern:

  • 2 x 12-hour day shifts
  • 2 x 12-hour night shifts
  • 4 days off

This rotation repeats continuously throughout the year.

title: Senior Software Product Manager
description:
We are hiring a Senior Software Product Manager to lead the next chapter of growth for our semiconductor software portfolio, with a primary focus on Fault Detection and Classification (FDC). This is a high-impact role for an AI-first product leader who thrives at the intersection of advanced manufacturing, sensor hardware, and modern B2B software. You will own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for innovative solutions that solve real, costly problems for our customers on the fab floor — and you will partner closely with our hardware and sensor teams to deliver experiences that no software-only competitor can match.

You bring senior-level product judgment, an energetic and positive mindset, and a relentless focus on customer outcomes. You operate fluently in Agile delivery, ground your thinking in Design Thinking and Lean Startup principles, and treat AI not as a feature but as a foundational capability that reshapes how products are built and how customers extract value.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

Product Strategy & Roadmap

  • Own the vision, strategy, and multi-quarter roadmap for one or more software products in the semiconductor FDC space.
  • Drive growth of existing products through innovative, differentiated capabilities — particularly those enabled by AI and machine learning.
  • Define and track product KPIs tied to customer outcomes (yield, uptime, time-to-detection, time-to-root-cause) and business outcomes (ARR, expansion, retention).

Customer Discovery & Problem Framing

  • Spend significant time with process engineers, equipment engineers, integration engineers, and fab IT to deeply understand workflows, pain points, and unmet needs.
  • Apply Design Thinking to frame problems from the customer's perspective before jumping to solutions.
  • Use Lean Startup methods — hypotheses, MVPs, and validated learning — to de-risk bets and accelerate the path from idea to customer value.

AI-First Product Development

  • Champion an AI-first approach: identify where AI/ML meaningfully improves detection, classification, prediction, and decision support over traditional rule-based methods.
  • Partner with data science and engineering to scope ML use cases, define data requirements, and design for explainability, trust, and operator adoption in a manufacturing setting.
  • Make pragmatic build/buy/partner decisions across the AI stack.

Sensor & Hardware Integration

  • Work directly with sensor hardware and instrumentation teams to ensure software products fully leverage upstream signal quality, sampling, and metadata.
  • Influence sensor product roadmaps where software-side requirements (data fidelity, latency, edge processing, protocols) unlock meaningful customer value.
  • Translate hardware capabilities into compelling software value propositions for fab customers.

Agile Delivery & Execution

  • Operate as the product owner within Agile teams — maintaining a prioritized, outcome-oriented backlog and clear acceptance criteria.
  • Partner with engineering, UX, QA, and DevOps to ship high-quality releases on a predictable cadence.
  • Balance discovery and delivery — keep the team running fast on committed work while continuously validating what comes next.

Go-to-Market & Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Partner with Sales, Application Engineering, Marketing, and Support to launch features, enable the field, and drive adoption.
  • Serve as the credible product voice with customers, partners, and internal executives — including roadmap reviews and strategic account engagements.

Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years at a senior level, in B2B software.

  • Demonstrated track record of growing existing products through innovation — not just managing a backlog, but moving the needle on adoption, expansion, and customer outcomes.

  • AI-first product thinking: experience scoping, shipping, and scaling AI/ML-powered capabilities in a B2B software product.

  • Strong working knowledge of Agile delivery, Design Thinking, and Lean Startup methodologies — and the judgment to know when to apply each.

  • Excellent customer discovery, written communication, and stakeholder management skills across technical and executive audiences.

  • Comfort working closely with hardware/firmware/sensor teams and translating physical-world data into software value.

  • Positive, energetic, growth-oriented mindset; thrives in ambiguity and brings clarity, optimism, and momentum to the team.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience with the semiconductor manufacturing process (front-end fab operations, process control, equipment data) — Fault Detection and Classification (FDC) experience strongly preferred.

  • Familiarity with industry standards and data ecosystems such as SEMI standards, SECS/GEM, EDA (Interface A), MES integration, and time-series sensor data at scale.

  • Experience launching products that combine on-premise, edge, and cloud deployment models in regulated or high-availability environments.

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, or a related technical field; advanced degree or MBA a plus.

The expected salary range for this position is between $120,000 and $160,000 annually. The actual compensation will be determined based on experience, location, and other factors permitted by law. In addition, INFICON employees are eligible for a profit-sharing bonus with a target of 10% as well as 401K match up to 8% (vesting schedule).

INFICON provides a dynamic work environment that promotes diversity, equity, and inclusion. Our employees experience ongoing green initiatives, flexible work hours, and a variety of health and wellness programs.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Event Streaming Systems
description:
About the Team

The Storage organization builds and operates the online stateful systems and abstractions that DoorDash Engineering depends on: reliable, efficient, secure, and easy to use. Within Storage, the Event Streaming Systems team owns the event streaming platform that powers business-critical, event-driven workflows across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo, including Kafka, our event streaming abstraction layer (internally called Event Bus), and the next generation of streaming platform technologies.

These systems sit on the Tier-0 critical path. They move trillions of events per day across multiple regions and underpin how hundreds of engineering teams build reliable, event-driven products at massive scale.

About the Role

We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to set the technical direction for our event streaming platform and lead its evolution over the next several years. This is a senior individual-contributor role: you'll operate as a force multiplier across teams, owning the hardest architectural problems, driving org-wide technical strategy, and raising the engineering bar for everyone who builds on and operates streaming infrastructure.

You'll go deep on the internals of modern streaming systems, from the Kafka protocol and storage engine to object-store-backed, diskless architectures like WarpStream and AutoMQ. You'll make the high-leverage bets that determine how DoorDash streams data for years to come, on a platform that serves hundreds of engineering teams and trillions of events per day.

You must be located in the New York Metro Area for this hybrid position. You will report to the Engineering Manager on our Event Streaming Systems team within the Storage organization.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

  • Set the multi-year technical vision and architecture for DoorDash's event streaming platform, and drive alignment in that direction across Storage, SRE, Data Platform, and Product Engineering.
  • Lead the largest and most ambiguous streaming initiatives end to end, such as re-architecting toward diskless, object-store-backed streaming to cut cost and operational overhead across the fleet.
  • Go deep on the internals of Kafka and modern streaming systems (WarpStream, AutoMQ, and similar), and use that depth to solve problems that block the rest of the organization.
  • Own architectural decisions with company-wide blast radius, from replication, consensus, and storage design to multi-region topology, capacity, and cost efficiency.
  • Debug and resolve the hardest distributed systems problems in production, including subtle correctness, performance, and reliability issues under Tier-0 constraints.
  • Raise the technical bar through design reviews, mentorship of senior engineers, and by establishing the standards and patterns others build on.
  • Partner with engineering leadership to shape roadmaps, make build-versus-buy and open-source-versus-managed decisions, and translate business needs into platform strategy.

We're excited about you because…

  • You have deep 8+ years of hands-on experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems in production, with a track record of technical leadership across multiple teams or an organization.
  • You have operated event streaming systems such as Kafka at scale, and you understand their internals, including the log storage engine, the ISR replication model, metadata consensus (KRaft/ZooKeeper), the consumer/producer protocol, partitioning, and rebalancing.
  • You are a strong engineer in Java, Go, or a similar language, with deep expertise in concurrency, distributed systems, and building reliable, maintainable production infrastructure.
  • You have led high-impact, cross-team initiatives from ambiguous problems to shipped outcomes, and you can influence technical direction across an organization without relying on authority.
  • You have strong fundamentals in Linux, networking, storage, and JVM-based systems, and you use them to reason about performance and failure modes from first principles.
  • You understand the trade-offs of object-store-backed streaming, including write-path latency versus cost, cross-AZ network cost avoidance, the separation of compute and storage, and object metadata and caching design.
  • You communicate with clarity and can bring engineers, managers, and leaders along on complex technical decisions and trade-offs.
  • You have proficiency in using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) in the full software development lifecycle, including designing, generating code, testing, monitoring and releasing software

Preferred

  • Experience with the internals of object-store-backed or diskless streaming architectures such as WarpStream or AutoMQ, or with tiered storage in Kafka.
  • Contributions to Kafka or related open-source distributed systems (Pulsar, Redpanda, or similar).
  • Experience with broker and JVM tuning, partition management, or Cruise Control at large scale.
  • Experience designing multi-region streaming platforms and reasoning about their consistency, durability, and cost trade-offs.
  • Experience leading migrations of Tier-0 infrastructure with zero customer-visible impact.
  • Experience driving significant efficiency or cost wins on large streaming or storage fleets.

title: Product Manager - Legal, Compliance & Invoicing
description:
Fourvenues

Fourvenues is a tech platform born from within the entertainment industry, which gives it a first-hand understanding of what venues actually need to run their business.

The platform brings everything under one roof: online ticket sales, guest list management, VIP reservations, a fully integrated POS system for the bar and box office, real-time capacity tracking, and a built-in CRM to truly understand your audience.

What makes it stand out is how it connects all these touchpoints, from the moment someone buys a ticket to what they spend at the bar, generating cross-referenced data that lets owners see exactly which events perform best, which customer profiles spend the most, which promoters actually deliver, and where money is being left on the table.

The result: smarter decisions, less manual work, tighter control over the business, and a smoother experience for both staff and guests.

Your Mission

Your mission will be to ensure that Fourvenues builds a legally robust, scalable product that is ready to operate across multiple markets.

You will be responsible for translating legal, tax and regulatory requirements into clear product decisions, actionable documentation, roadmap priorities, and well-coordinated developments across Technology, Finance, Sales, Customer Success and other Product domains.

We are not looking for a traditional in-house lawyer, but for a Product Manager who can understand regulation, coordinate external legal advisors, and turn legal uncertainty into practical product solutions.

What You'll Be Doing

This role will be part of the Product team and will work closely with Technology, Finance, Sales, Customer Success and the Leadership team.

It will play a key role in the company's growth, supporting expansion into new markets and the development of new product lines without compromising the platform's quality, scalability or legal compliance.

title: Research Scientist
description:
Required Qualifications\: (as evidenced by an attached resume)

● Ph.D (or foreign equivalent) in computer science, computational science, data science, applied mathematics, engineering, physical or life sciences, or a closely related field.

● Three (3) years of research experience using computational, data-driven, or AI/ML methods, to include at least one year of research experience following attainment of a Doctoral degree or foreign equivalent.

● Hands-on experience applying machine learning or artificial intelligence to research or technical problems, including model training, evaluation, or deployment.

● Programming experience in Python using scientific computing, data analysis, or machine learning libraries.

● Experience with at least one AI/ML framework or ecosystem, such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, scikit-learn, Spark/MLlib, or Hugging Face.

● Experience with Linux-based research computing or high-performance computing, including command-line tools and batch or interactive workflows.

● Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work with researchers across multiple disciplines.

Preferred Qualifications\:

● Familiarity with parallel or accelerator-based computing, including GPUs, distributed computing, MPI, OpenMP, CUDA, ROCm, or related technologies.

● Experience using GPUs or other accelerators for machine learning, deep learning, or scientific computing.

● Experience with generative AI or large language models, including deploying, running, or optimizing LLMs on local GPU or CPU hardware.

● Experience with distributed or multi-GPU model training, inference, profiling, or performance optimization.

● Experience with programming in high-performance computing languages such as C, C++, or Fortran.

● Familiarity with research-computing software and workflow tools such as Slurm, containers, Conda, or Spack.

● Experience with reproducible machine learning workflows, including data preparation, model training, evaluation, and management of software environments.

● Experience developing technical documentation, tutorials, workshops, or other training materials for researchers and students.

● Experience contributing to collaborative research projects, open-source software, publications, or research proposals.

The Institute for Advanced Computational Science (IACS) at Stony Brook University (SBU) is seeking an early-career Research Scientist to join a new Tier-1 supercomputing center funded by the National Science Foundation (NSF).

The IACS is an interdisciplinary research center at Stony Brook University focused on applying computational methods to address a variety of scientific questions. IACS provides computational infrastructure and technical expertise to researchers across the university and beyond.

AMA27/Kitsune, a new NSF-funded Tier-1 supercomputing center, will support large-scale research in artificial intelligence and machine learning, data science, computational physics, climate science, biomedical research, materials science, and other data- and compute-intensive fields. AMA27/Kitsune will be a central resource of the Stony Brook Supercomputing Center (SBSC).

The Research Scientist will work with faculty, students, researchers, and research-computing staff on AI/ML, data science, computational science, and computer science applications. The position is intended for an early-career scientist who wants to develop deeper expertise in AI/ML and high-performance computing while helping researchers run reliable and reproducible workflows on the supercomputing platform. All work must follow the policies and procedures of SBSC, IACS, Stony Brook University, and the National Science Foundation.

The position provides hands-on experience with AI/ML software, GPU and high performance computing, and large-scale research computing.

Primary Purpose\:

The Research Scientist will work with users across scientific disciplines, with particular emphasis on AI/ML workloads and research workflows. Responsibilities include\:

● Work with researchers to develop, run, troubleshoot, and improve AI/ML, data science, and computational workflows.

● Teach users how to work with machine learning frameworks, GPU-enabled computing, reproducible software environments, and the supercomputing platform.

● Assist with model training and inference, data processing, software configuration, debugging, benchmarking, and performance analysis on HPC systems.

● Learn and apply SBSC tools and operational practices and follow applicable requirements for research activities and data management.

The role provides substantial hands-on work with modern AI/ML software stacks and large-scale computing in support of the national research community.

Job Duties\:

● Support AI/ML and scientific applications on the supercomputing platform. Install and configure software, assist with model training and inference, debug problems, benchmark workloads, analyze performance, and help users make effective use of GPU and other accelerator resources.

● Work with faculty, researchers, students, and research-computing staff to develop and improve AI/ML, data science, and computational workflows. Assist with data preparation, reproducibility, scaling, and efficient use of shared computing resources.

● Provide user support and training through technical consultations, documentation, tutorials, office hours, workshops, and presentations. Teach researchers how to use AI/ML frameworks and research-computing tools effectively.

● Test, troubleshoot, and maintain research software environments, including machine learning libraries, containers, compilers, schedulers, and related tools. Develop and maintain technical documentation and web resources.

● Contribute to project coordination, reports, presentations, publications, and research or training proposals under the guidance of senior staff and faculty.

Special Notes\:
The Research Foundation of SUNY is a private educational corporation. Employment is subject to the Research Foundation policies and procedures, sponsor guidelines and the availability of funding. FLSA Exempt position, not eligible for the overtime provisions of the FLSA. Minimum salary threshold must be met to maintain FLSA exemption.

Resume/CV and cover letter should be included with the online application.

title: Director of Information Technology
description:
Overview

Join a team where innovation meets mission. Our AI, cloud, cyber, and modernization solutions save agencies thousands of hours, safeguard national security, and strengthen health and humanitarian missions worldwide. With 1,700+ team members, 1,500+ AI/data experts, and 100+ prime contracts, we deliver at scale and with purpose.

We’ve been recognized as a Top Workplace by the Washington Post for six straight years and named to the Inc. 5000 Fastest Growing Private Companies 13 of the past 14 years. Credence is a welcoming home for those looking to grow and contribute to positive change. We encourage all employees to expand beyond their boundaries, dive into important world-changing Federal challenges.

Position Summary

Senior technology leader to provide enterprise-wide direction and operational leadership for the company's internal information technology function while also contributing technical expertise to selected customer opportunities and engagements. This role is accountable for the strategy, security, reliability, scalability, and business value of the technology environment supporting approximately 1,500 employees, including responsible adoption of artificial intelligence across the enterprise.

The successful candidate will combine executive-level judgment with current technical credibility. The role will lead a team of approximately 16 IT professionals, translate business priorities into a practical technology roadmap, strengthen cybersecurity and operational discipline, and ensure that employees have secure, dependable, and effective technology services.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to the duties listed below

Enterprise Technology Strategy and Governance

• Develop and execute an enterprise IT strategy and multi-year roadmap aligned with company growth, workforce needs, operational priorities, customer commitments, and risk tolerance.

• Serve as the principal advisor to executive leadership on technology investment, architecture, cybersecurity risk, operational resilience, emerging capabilities, and technology enabled business improvement.

• Establish clear governance, architecture standards, policies, decision rights, and lifecycle practices for infrastructure, cloud services, enterprise applications, data, end-user technology, and technology vendors.

• Create a disciplined investment process that balances modernization, security, service quality, technical debt, scalability, and total cost of ownership.

• Define meaningful service, risk, financial, and delivery metrics; communicate performance, priorities, tradeoffs, and emerging issues to senior leadership in business terms.

Artificial Intelligence Strategy and Enterprise Adoption

• Define and communicate a clear Credence vision for the role of artificial intelligence in the company's business, workforce, and operating model, giving leaders and employees a consistent message about priorities, opportunities, expectations, and responsible use.

• Develop and execute an enterprise AI strategy and roadmap that embeds practical AI capabilities into core workflows, improves productivity and decision-making, and supports scalable growth.

• Partner with business and functional leaders to identify high-value use cases, prioritize pilots and investments, redesign workflows, measure results, and scale successful solutions.

• Establish AI governance and guardrails addressing security, privacy, data protection, legal and contractual compliance, acceptable use, human oversight, vendor selection, and risk.

• Build organizational AI literacy and adoption through executive engagement, employee communication, training, change leadership, communities of practice, and accessible support.

IT Operations, Infrastructure, and Service Delivery

• Lead the internal IT organization and provide accountable oversight of service desk operations, endpoint services, identity and access, networks, collaboration platforms, cloud and hosting environments, enterprise applications, integrations, asset management, and related support services.

• Ensure reliable and secure day-to-day operations through mature incident, problem, request, change, configuration, release, and knowledge-management practices.

• Establish service expectations and operating measures that improve responsiveness, user experience, availability, capacity, and accountability across a geographically distributed workforce.

• Guide modernization of legacy platforms and adoption of cloud, automation, infrastructure-as-code, monitoring, data, and AI-enabled capabilities when they provide clear business value and manageable risk.

• Maintain effective business continuity, disaster recovery, backup, crisis response, and technology resilience capabilities; periodically test plans and close identified gaps.

• Own IT financial planning, forecasting, procurement, software and license optimization, vendor performance, contract management, and the business cases for significant technology investments.

Cybersecurity, Compliance, and Risk

• Provide executive accountability for the protection of corporate systems, information, and technology assets in coordination with cybersecurity, compliance, legal, contracts, and business leadership.

• Maintain a risk-based security program appropriate for a federal contractor, including identity governance, access control, vulnerability and patch management, security monitoring, incident response, third-party risk, data protection, and employee awareness.

• Ensure internal technology practices support applicable federal cybersecurity frameworks, contractual requirements, audits, assessments, and customer security expectations.

• Brief executives on material technology and cybersecurity risks, recommend mitigation priorities, and ensure corrective actions are owned, funded, tracked, and completed.

Leadership and Organizational Development

• Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team of approximately 16 IT professionals; establish clear accountability, service ownership, succession plans, and development pathways.

• Design the organization, staffing model, sourcing approach, and partner ecosystem needed to support current operations and future growth.

• Build trusted relationships across business functions, listen closely to internal customers, and lead change with clear communication and practical adoption support.

• Create a culture of service, security, documentation, continuous improvement, collaboration, and responsible innovation.

Customer-Facing Technology Leadership

• Serve as a senior technical advisor or delivery leader on selected customer engagements, particularly those involving enterprise IT modernization, cloud, cybersecurity, DevSecOps, data, AI, infrastructure, or managed services.

• Support capture and proposal efforts by shaping technical approaches, reviewing solution architectures, contributing written content, participating in color-team reviews, and presenting in customer meetings or oral proposals.

• Help translate customer missions and requirements into feasible, secure, and differentiated solutions that reflect delivery realities, compliance obligations, cost, schedule, and risk.

• Provide technical oversight, independent reviews, issue resolution, or executive sponsorship for strategically important programs when requested.

• Connect lessons, talent, tools, and reusable capabilities across corporate IT and customer delivery while maintaining appropriate boundaries between internal and customer environments.

Requirements

• Bachelor's degree in information technology, computer science, engineering, management information systems, or a related field are required; equivalent combinations of education and relevant experience may be considered.

• Active federal security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain one; a current Secret, Top Secret, or TS/SCI clearance is advantageous but not required.

• Typically, 15 or more years of progressive technology experience, including at least 7 years leading technical teams, programs, or functions with increasing organizational scope and accountability are required.

• Must have demonstrated ability to set enterprise technology strategy and to lead reliable day-to-day operations in a growing, geographically distributed organization.

• Must have broad technical understanding across enterprise infrastructure, networks, cloud platforms, identity and access management, endpoint computing, enterprise applications, IT service management, cybersecurity, data protection, resilience, and systems integration.

• Must have experience managing budgets, forecasts, vendors, contracts, licenses, staffing, and investment priorities, with the ability to connect technology decisions to business outcomes.

• Must have experience communicating with executive leaders and presenting complex technical, financial, and risk matters clearly to nontechnical audiences.

• Must have demonstrated success building and developing teams, establishing operating discipline, leading organizational change, and earning trust across functions.

• Must have experience supporting customers in a consultative, solutioning, program leadership, or technical delivery capacity.

Leadership Competencies

• Enterprise perspective and business judgment

• Strategic thinking paired with practical execution

• Technical credibility and intellectual curiosity

• Executive communication and influence

• Customer and employee service orientation

• Cybersecurity and risk ownership

• Financial and vendor management discipline

• Talent development, collaboration, and accountability

• Calm, decisive leadership during incidents and periods of change

Preferred Qualifications

• Leadership experience within a federal government contractor, technology services firm, or similarly regulated and security-sensitive organization.

• Experience supporting federal civilian, defense, intelligence, or national security customers and familiarity with federal acquisition, delivery, security, and authorization environments.

• Experience leading enterprise cloud migration, hybrid cloud, Zero Trust, DevSecOps, automation, organization-wide AI adoption, data, or large-scale modernization initiatives.

• Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CCSP, AWS or Microsoft Azure architecture credentials, ITIL, PMP, or comparable credentials.

• Master's degree in a relevant technical or business discipline.

Work Environment and Other Requirements

This position operates in a professional office and technology environment and may support employees and operations across multiple locations. The role may require periodic travel, customer meetings, and availability outside normal business hours for significant incidents, continuity events, or planned technology changes. The incumbent must handle sensitive company and customer information with discretion and comply with applicable security requirements.

Credence will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with applicable law. This description summarizes the general nature and level of work and is not an exhaustive list of responsibilities, duties, or qualifications. Responsibilities may change as business needs evolve

Salary Range: $130,000 - $150,000 annually. Actual compensation will be determined based on the selected candidate's experience, education, certifications, skills, and overall qualifications.

Benefits

  • Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
  • Retirement Plan (401k, IRA)
  • Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary & AD&D)
  • Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick & Public Holidays)
  • Family Leave (Maternity, Paternity)
  • Short Term & Long Term Disability
  • Training & Development

title: Portfolio Analyst
location: Crown Way, Cardiff, CF14 3UZ; Queen Elizabeth House, 1 Sibbald Walk, Edinburgh, EH8 8FT; Erskine House, 20-32 Chichester Street, Belfast, BT1 4GF
description:
• Job grade: Senior Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: CH - Transformation Delivery - Portfolio Delivery and Change
  • Type of role: Business Management and Improvement, Project Delivery, Other
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Part-time, Compressed hours
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Crown Way, Cardiff, CF14 3UZ; Queen Elizabeth House, 1 Sibbald Walk, Edinburgh, EH8 8FT; Erskine House, 20-32 Chichester Street, Belfast, BT1 4GF

About the job

Job summary

Are you an experienced Portfolio Analyst who wants to play a key role in delivering change that matters? Do you enjoy turning portfolio data into meaningful insight that drives better decisions?

If so, you could be our new Portfolio Analyst at Companies House!

As a Portfolio Analyst, you will play a key role in ensuring the right change is delivered at the right time and in the right way across Companies House. Providing vital portfolio insight, governance and control, you will help support the successful delivery of strategic programmes and projects that contribute to organisational priorities.

Working closely with stakeholders across the business, you will maintain a clear and accurate view of the delivery portfolio, ensuring plans, dependencies, risks, issues and resource requirements are effectively managed, monitored and reported. Through high-quality portfolio reporting, strong governance practices and the effective use of Portfolio and Project Management (PPM) tools, you will help create a trusted single source of information that enables informed decision-making and successful delivery outcomes.

This role sits within the Portfolio Delivery and Change Directorate, which is responsible for portfolio management, programme and project delivery, and change management across Companies House. The Directorate's vision is to deliver the right change, at the right time, in the right way, ensuring people remain at the heart of change and that investment delivers lasting value for the organisation.

We are a dynamic, professional and inclusive team that values collaboration, continuous improvement and delivering meaningful outcomes. As a Portfolio Analyst, you will contribute to strengthening organisational capability, supporting strategic objectives and helping Companies House achieve its ambition of providing trusted and transparent services for the UK economy.

Why choose Companies House?

At Companies House we take a proactive approach to wellbeing by promoting a welcoming culture, healthy work life balance and supporting colleagues to be their best in work because we know people are the key to our success.

Our benefits include:

  • Flexible working with no core hours (between 6am and 8pm)
  • 30 days annual leave
  • 8 bank holidays & 1 privilege day
  • Enrolment into the Civil Service Pension scheme, with an average employer contribution of 28%

Find out more about what a great place Companies House is to work.

Job description

Our Portfolio Analyst will be involved with:

Delivery and Leadership

  • Assist and support their line manager, deputising when necessary.
  • Champion the use of best practice project, programme and portfolio management standards and processes.

Resourcing

  • Engage with stakeholders across Companies House on portfolio resource management requirements.
  • Collect timely and accurate data to report on portfolio resource requirements.

Governance, Reporting and Assurance

  • Analyse and challenge portfolio and programme reporting data and escalate as required.
  • Monitor and control the baseline of key portfolio milestones.
  • Escalate where milestone changes are anticipated to the Portfolio Reporting and Insights lead.
  • Provide accurate and timely data required to maintain the Portfolio Delivery Plan.
  • Provide reporting, including milestone look ahead and other reports, as required.
  • Support the monthly reporting process for the Companies House Portfolio Guidance and Support.
  • Develop and share best practice on project management processes, tools and templates, and benchmarks against industry standard.
  • Provide guidance and training to the project delivery community and other stakeholders on scheduling best practice.

Planning and Scheduling

  • Maintain, monitor and continuously improve the Portfolio Delivery Plan.
  • Recognise, record and track key portfolio dependencies.
  • Maintain PPM tooling to ensure one source of the truth is always accurate and utilised.
  • Provide SME support in scheduling to Project Managers.
  • Assuring the quality of project schedules and scheduling contents of business cases.
  • Setting and maintaining project schedule baselines.

Project Pipeline

  • Work with SROs and Project Managers to ensure that information on the project pipeline is accurate and up to date.

Risk and Opportunity Management

  • Help to maintain the Portfolio RAID log. Identify portfolio risks (threats and opportunities) and raise as appropriate.

Stakeholder Management

  • Manage and engage with a wide range of internal stakeholders.

Please note:

  • You will be based at either our Cardiff, Edinburgh or Belfast office where you will be expected to attend on a regular basis.
  • Companies House cannot offer Visa sponsorship to candidates through this campaign.
  • This is a full time position, however, we are able to accept applications from those looking to work part time - a minimum of 30 hours/4 days per week, or those looking to work compressed hours.

About the team

The Portfolio Delivery and Change Directorate is responsible for enabling the successful delivery of Companies House strategic priorities through effective portfolio management (PMO), programme and project delivery and change management. Our vision is to deliver the right change, at the right time, in the right way, empowering people to maximise benefits and achieve our strategy. This means putting people at the heart of everything we do, delivering change collaboratively and effectively, and ensuring that investment in change creates lasting value for the organisation.

Person specification

We're looking for an experienced Portfolio Analyst, who can demonstrate:

  • Working in a PMO or project/portfolio management environment.
  • Planning, scheduling, finance, and risk management in a project, programme or portfolio environment.
  • A proven track record of delivery and continuous improvement.
  • Proactively planning and prioritising work and managing multiple activities in order to meet deadlines.
  • Using Excel and PowerBI.
  • Working unsupervised and taking initiative.
  • The ability to work flexibly across a range of priorities and deliver quality outcomes.

Find out more about the Government Project Delivery capability framework (PDCF).

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Seeing the Big Picture
  • Changing and Improving
  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Working Together

Technical skills

We'll assess you against these technical skills during the selection process:

  • Resource management: The ability to identify, profile, secure and manage the resources required to deliver the work (Working level).

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £48,147, Companies House contributes £13,948 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

We believe that our success is driven by the well-being and satisfaction of our team members at all levels of the organisation. At Companies House we’re committed to providing a comprehensive benefits package that goes beyond the ordinary, ensuring your career journey with us is not only fulfilling, but also rewarding. We pride ourselves on offering a quality work-life balance with our employee wellbeing being central to our working practices.

Head to Our benefits - Working for us - Recruitment (companieshouse.gov.uk) to find out more about the fantastic benefits package we have at Companies House.

We celebrate diversity...

As an equal opportunity employer, we celebrate diversity, being committed to ensuring we’re representative of the citizens we serve and creating an inclusive environment. Everyone in Companies House brings something different, and so will you. To fulfil our commitment to recruiting and attracting diverse talent we welcome applications from underrepresented groups. We also welcome applications from Welsh speakers.

We are proud to be a disability confident leader. Our recruitment process is fully inclusive and we can make adjustments as needed through our process. These could include having an interview buddy, extra time at interviews/assessments and receiving interview questions in advance, to name a few.

If you require any reasonable adjustments at application stage, or if you'd like to discuss any person-centred adjustments, please contact us by emailing recruitmentCH@companieshouse.gov.uk.

Read our 'Applying under the Disability Confidence Scheme (DCS)' guide to find out how to successfully complete an application under the Disability Confidence Scheme (DCS).

Where will you be working?

You will be based at either our Cardiff, Edinburgh or Belfast office where you will be expected to attend on a regular basis. We are currently using a hybrid approach to the way we work which provides opportunities for you to be adaptable in the way you work so that you can achieve a healthy balance between your work and home life. The degree of choice you have will depend on your role and your day-to-day work activities. Your manager will agree regular patterns of attendance with you, however you may be required to make yourself available to attend the office more frequently when required to meet business needs. Please be aware that this role can only be worked in the UK and not overseas.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours, Strengths, Experience and Technical skills.

Key dates (dates are indicative only and could be subject to change)

  • Closing date - 8th November 2026, at 23:55
  • Sifting - w/c 9th November 2026
  • Interviews - w/c 23rd November 2026, on Microsoft Teams

Communications will be electronic via email therefore it is important that you check your Civil Service Jobs account regularly, as well as your spam/junk email folder.

What will the process look like?

1. Application

During the application and sift stages we will be using the Success Profiles: Experience.

In your application form we’d like you to:

  1. Tell us about your employment history, including any key responsibilities and achievements.
  2. Write a 1000 word personal statement where you demonstrate how you meet the skills required for this role, providing examples to evidence your level of experience. In your personal statement we are looking for evidence of:
  • Working in a PMO or project/portfolio management environment.
  • Planning, scheduling, finance, and risk management in a project, programme or portfolio environment.
  • A proven track record of delivery and continuous improvement.

We’re committed to being diverse and inclusive, so please make your application anonymous by removing all identifying personal information (such as names and dates) from your employment history and personal statement.

You should aim to make use of the full wordcount in each section of your application and show how you meet the above criteria. Please give clear and specific examples of what you have done personally and the impact it has had.

Further guidance on how to write your personal statement can be found here.

2. Sift

Once the advert has closed we will sift applications - this involves reading through them all, please bear with us as this can take some time. The panel will look at all elements of your application for evidence of the sift criteria.

We may raise the score required if we receive a high number of applications. We may also choose to take through the highest performing candidates to the next stage. If, after the final stage is completed and roles are unfilled, we will proceed to invite lower scoring candidates to interview.

Also, if we receive a high volume of applications, we may carry out a pre-sift and will look at your application for evidence of: Working in a PMO or project/portfolio management environment. Those applications which are successful at pre-sift stage will then progress to the main sift, where we'll read and score the rest of your application.

3. Interview

Successful candidates from the sift stage will be invited to attend a virtual interview, which will be conducted using Microsoft Teams.

Companies House uses a blended interview technique, allowing us to find out more about you. We use the Success Profile framework and during the interview stage we will be assessing Behaviours, Strengths, Technical, and Experience.

The interview will include:

1) Activity - This will be a presentation which we'll ask candidates to prepare in advance. This will assess Experience: Working in a PMO or project/portfolio management environment. More details on this will be sent to candidates who are invited to interview.

2) Main panel Q&A - after the activity segment, we'll move onto the main Q&A section of the interview where candidates will be asked questions relating to:

  • Behaviours: Seeing the Big Picture, Changing and Improving, Communicating and Influencing, Working Together
  • Strengths: Not shared in advance as we want to see your first, natural response.
  • Technical: Resource Management.

4 . Offer

Once all interviews have been completed, you will be notified of the outcome. Offers will be made in strict merit order. The lead criteria to distinguish between tied candidates will Experience: Working in a PMO or project/portfolio management environment.

A reserve list may be held for up to 12 months from which further appointments may be made for the same or similar roles (of the same or lower grade). Subject to business need, if a suitable position opens during this time we may reach out to individuals in merit order.

Our recruitment process is underpinned by the principle of recruitment based on fair and open competition with decisions made on the basis of merit, as outlined in the Civil Service Commissioners’ Recruitment Principles.

Security

Successful candidates must pass a Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) check before they can be appointed.

BPSS is an entry level security check. It uses the Police National Computer (PNC) to make sure a candidate has no convictions. The check returns evidence of any current criminal record and un-spent convictions under the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974.

Sponsorship

Companies House cannot offer Visa sponsorship to candidates through this campaign. Companies House holds a Visa sponsorship licence but this can only be used for certain roles and this campaign does not qualify. Should you apply for this role and require sponsorship, your application may be rejected, and any provisional offers of employment withdrawn.

Pre-Employment Checking

In line with Government guidance, successfully appointed candidates will need to provide documents for our Right to Work checks.

From June 2026, applicants who are successful at interview will be, as part of pre-employment screening, subject to a check on the Internal Fraud Database (IFD). Your personal details (name, National Insurance number, and date of birth) will be checked against the Civil Service Resourcing Extract IFD.

This check will provide information about employees who have been dismissed for fraud or dishonesty offences. This check also applies to employees who resign or otherwise leave before being dismissed for fraud or dishonesty had their employment continued.

If your details appear on this database, you will not be offered employment unless you can demonstrate exceptional circumstances. Companies House, acting on behalf of the vacancy holder, will inform you if your application is refused for this reason.

Please note: You are not eligible to apply for a role within the Civil Service if the application is made within a 5 year period following a dismissal for carrying out internal fraud against government.

Nationality statement

As part of our recruitment process, it is essential for all candidates to independently verify their eligibility to work in the UK before applying. This includes a thorough check of your right to work to ensure compliance with UK employment laws, being mindful of the recent changes to going rates detailed on GOV.UK.

Please ensure you have the necessary documentation and permissions in place. Our team is dedicated to fostering a diverse and inclusive workforce and encourages applicants from all backgrounds to apply. However, it is the candidate's responsibility to ensure they meet the UK's legal requirements to work.



Feedback will only be provided if you attend an interview or assessment.

Security

Nationality requirements

This job is broadly open to the following groups:

  • UK nationals

title: NOC Senior Engineer
description:
Company Introduction

Availity is one of the leading health information networks in the United States, processing more than 4 billion transactions annually and connecting more than two million healthcare providers and over two thousand technology partners to health plans nationwide. Our teams of technology, business, and customer service professionals in Bangalore, India, are working together to transform healthcare delivery in the United States through innovation and collaboration. Our technologists help develop cutting-edge revenue cycle solutions that help hospitals, health systems, and physicians maximize payments and optimize their workflows.

Availity is a diverse group of people whose talents, curiosity and passion steer the company to create innovative solutions for the US Healthcare industry. If you are a driven, creative and collaborative individual, with exceptional technology skills to drive innovation, we want to hear from you.

Job Description

The NOC Senior Engineer is a senior, hands-on operations role focused on running a mature 24×7 Network Operations Center. This position is responsible for advanced incident
management, cross-domain technical escalation, proactive monitoring maturity, and ensuring operational stability across network, server, cloud, and database platforms. The role acts as the senior technical authority on shift and ensures disciplined NOC execution and follow-the-sun continuity.

Roles & Responsibilities

Must Have Skills:

  • L3 escalation for P1/P2 incidents
  • Multi-cloud (AWS & Azure) expertise
  • Advanced Linux & Windows administration
  • Kubernetes & EKS operational expertise
  • Cloud networking & security
  • Alert tuning & dashboard ownership
  • Terraform & automation
  • Shift leadership & mentoring

Good to Have Skills :

  • AWS Solutions Architect – Professional
  • Azure Solutions Architect Expert
  • Kubernetes CKA
  • SRE / reliability engineering exposure
  • ITIL Foundation

Eligibility

Advanced NOC Responsibilities

  • Act as the L3 technical escalation point and senior authority for P1/P2 incidents.
  • Lead real-time incident triage, stabilization, and restoration during major outages.
  • Execute and enforce incident command practices including ownership, timelines, and escalation control.
  • Collaborate with Operations Center (OC) and Incident Managers during Major Incident Management (MIM).
  • Ensure accurate, real-time updates and complete post-incident documentation in ITSM tools.
  • Enforce adherence to NOC SOPs, runbooks, alert response standards, and escalation matrices.

Proactive Monitoring & Operational Excellence:

  • Own the effectiveness of proactive monitoring across all infrastructure layers.
  • Identify alert noise, gaps, and false positives; drive alert tuning and threshold optimization.
  • Improve dashboards, service health views, and early-warning indicators.
  • Analyze recurring incidents and drive corrective and preventive actions to reduce MTTD and MTTR.

Shift Leadership & Continuity:

  • Serve as the senior technical lead during assigned shifts.
  • Lead structured shift handovers and overlapping coverage between global teams.
  • Mentor L2 and junior engineers during incidents and day-to-day operations.
  • Drive cross-skilling and raise overall NOC technical maturity.

Technical Requirements:

  • Cloud Platforms: Advanced operational experience in multi-cloud environments (AWS and Azure).
  • Server Engineering: Expert-level Linux and Windows server administration,troubleshooting, patching, and performance analysis.
  • Network Engineering Knowledge: Strong understanding of VPC/VNet architecture, subnets, routing tables, DNS, load balancers, firewalls, security groups/NSGs, and connectivity troubleshooting.
  • Database Operations: Solid operational knowledge of cloud databases (AWS RDS/Aurora, Azure SQL); performance symptoms, replication, failover, and availability concepts.
  • Kubernetes & Containers: Operational expertise with Kubernetes (EKS), container orchestration, node/pod health, and workload stability.
  • Automation & Infrastructure as Code: Hands-on experience executing and validating Terraform-based changes and scripted remediations.
  • Observability & Tooling: Strong hands-on experience with CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, Splunk, Grafana/Prometheus, and ITSM tools such as ServiceNow or Jira.

Required Experience:

  • 7–10 years of experience in advanced NOC, SRE, Cloud Operations, or Infrastructure Support roles.
  • Demonstrated advanced skills in multi-cloud environments, automation, and incident management.
  • Proven experience serving as a technical escalation point for complex, cross-domain issues.
  • Experience operating in 24×7, follow-the-sun NOC environments.

Preferred Certifications:

  • AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional
  • Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert
  • Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA)
  • ITIL Foundation (preferred)

Shift Model:

  • 24×7 rotational shifts with structured handovers, overlap coverage, and escalation Ownership

Video Camera Usage:

Availity fosters a collaborative and open culture where communication and engagement are central to our success. As a remote first company, we are also camera-first and provide all associates with camera/video capability to simulate the office environment. If you are not able to use your camera for all virtual meetings, you should not apply for this role.

Having cameras on helps create a more connected, interactive, and productive environment, allowing teams to communicate more effectively and build stronger working relationships. The usage of cameras also enhances security and protects sensitive company information. Video participation is required to ensure that only authorized personnel are present in meetings and to prevent unauthorized access, data breaches, preventing social engineering, or the sharing of confidential information with non-participants.

title: Senior Product Manager, AI Harness
description:
Who We Are


Verily Health is a data platform and technology company purpose-built to power AI-enabled precision health solutions that accelerate research and improve care for individuals and communities. Uniquely positioned at the intersection of technology, data science, and healthcare, Verily transforms multimodal health data into insights, models, and actions that make healthcare more personalized, predictive, and precise.

Description


Verily Health builds healthcare solutions for customers in every vertical in the market from life sciences to health systems to health plans and to patients. Each of those solutions is powered by AI capabilities. where we need to continually verify that the output is meeting the needs of our end users.


You’ll own the product strategy for Verily’s AI Evaluation Harness, the capabilities that first- and third-party AI developers use to benchmark, evaluate, monitor, and improve AI in healthcare. It spans golden-dataset evals, code assertions, LLM-as-a-judge evals, error analysis, and customer feedback signals, from quick one-off checks to long-running validation for regulated use.


You’ll set a 12-month strategy and a longer vision for what evaluation becomes in healthcare, then lead a team of software engineers and AI developers, working beside them every day, to build it. The standard you set will shape how trustworthy healthcare AI gets made at Verily and beyond. We’re looking for someone who has built evaluation products before and wants to define how the healthcare industry does it.


Responsibilities


  • Build a platform, not a point solution. Build evaluation tools for AI developers across many customers, verticals and clinical risk levels.
  • Obsess about user value. Name your end users, map their journeys, deeply understand their unmet needs, and conduct continuous discovery, delivery, and iteration with your team. You are directly responsible for end to end user value creation.
  • Build on Platform with technical credibility. Work as a peer with software architects, engineers, and data scientists on architecture and AI tradeoffs. Align solutions with Verily’s existing platform capabilities, and work with other teams to extend those capabilities in ways that scale the platform rather than create one-offs. Align with subject matter experts across clinical, regulatory, quality, security, and data science to right-size and de-risk solutions for the business constraints we must operate within.
  • Own product strategy and prioritization. Develop and communicate at different levels of detail and time horizon based on the audience; 12-month product strategy, half-year milestones, quarterly delivery roadmap, and biweekly sprint priorities. Set the direction, sequence the steps, and stay hands-on with the scrum team.
  • Own the AI Evaluation Harness portfolio. Drive the roadmap across error analysis, golden datasets, code assertions, LLM-as-a-judge, and customer feedback signals, and align stakeholders when interests conflict.

Qualifications


Minimum Qualifications


  • 5+ years of product management on platform products. You have been embedded with engineering scrum teams, and have a record of shipping and operating the product, not just specifying it.
  • Hands-on AI Evaluation product experience. You have shipped AI evaluation tooling that customers use (LLM-as-a-judge frameworks, golden datasets, code assertions and trace tooling). You can name the products, describe in detail the hard problems you solved, and show the adoption and quality outcomes for end users.
  • Deep technical foundation. You have a background in software engineering, systems engineering, data science, clinical informatics, or a comparable discipline. You can review architecture with engineers and go deep on LLM behavior with data scientists and be technically credible with them.
  • Stakeholder negotiation. You have aligned technical and non-technical leaders around one product vision, and can give examples where you moved a conflicted group to a decision.
  • Scale and complexity. You have owned a multi-tenant, version-controlled platform in a high-growth environment, with real tenancy, versioning, and backward-compatibility tradeoffs.

Preferred Qualifications


  • Healthcare domain fluency: FHIR resources, clinical informatics, and interoperability standards. You know what a “correct” clinical output requires and who must sign off on it.
  • Regulated environments: experience navigating HIPAA, GxP, FDA SaMD, or other healthcare compliance frameworks, ideally including building validation or audit evidence into a product.
  • Clinical Specific AI - Experience building evals for clinical or high-stakes AI outputs (summarization, coding, triage, decision support), including clinician-in-the-loop labeling and adjudication.

Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to work in Canada. Verily is currently unable to offer employment-based visa or work permit sponsorship for this position.


Compensation Information


The CAN base salary range for this full-time position is $132,500-$149,000 + bonus + equity + benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for the position across all US locations.
