Location

Forestry England Halwill Office, Beaworthy, Devon

About the job

Job summary

What you’ll do

The Wild Area Officer will oversee the development and delivery of the Wild Culm project in West District, managing progression through the different project stages, and facilitating their effective implementation on the ground. The post holder will be responsible for bringing the concept of wild areas to life, delivering at scale and pace to meet Forestry England’s ambitions for nature recovery. The project focuses on restoring the natural processes that underpin healthy habitats and species. Working closely with stakeholders, we will make bold management decisions that enhance these processes, strengthen ecosystem service provision, and maintain sustainable timber production, through adaptive silviculture and natural process led land management.

Where you’ll work

Covering the entire 3000 ha North Devon Beat, the project encompasses a clustered network of woodlands within the Culm National Character Area.

The post-holder will be based at Forestry England's Halwill Office in Devon (EX21 5UX).

Job description

Key responsibilities & accountabilities

1. Project Management

• Lead on the development of the project plan for the Wild Culm project
• Apply appropriate project management principles to ensure effective and timely project implementation, in accordance with Forest Wilding Programme guidance and framework
• Produce, maintain and review relevant project documentation throughout the project lifecycles.
• Develop annual and long-term work programmes and budgets for the projects, supported by relevant project boards and the Forest Wilding Programme Team.
• Manage a delegated budget to ensure the projects are managed within budgetary limits and fiscal guidelines.
• Support funding bids for external funding and ensure that commitments to funders for the projects are appropriately met through project delivery.
• Work with the Wild Areas Manager and Wild Area projects to ensure that programme, corporate and funder reporting requirements are met.

2. Land Management

• Lead on the development of a land management plan for the Wild Culm project, working with district colleagues and the Forest Wilding Programme Team to drive nature recovery at the landscape scale
• Lead the investigation of appropriate techniques which will deliver the vision for Wild Culm in restoring natural processes, ensuring there is a sound evidence base for land management interventions
• Implement agreed land management plans on the ground, including for example, installation of grazing infrastructure, management of herbivores, forest management, tree planting, peatland restoration, hydrological restoration.
• Procure and manage contracts, services and contractors, including graziers, forestry contractors, consultants and academic institutions.
• Ensure Forestry England procurement and contract management regulations are followed throughout the project
• Support the investigation of the (re)introduction of influential species to wild areas, which help restore natural processes.

3. Knowledge and Monitoring

• Support the implementation of Forestry England’s evidence framework, in assembling evidence to support decision-making and monitoring the success of land management interventions for nature recovery.
• Work with the national Forest Wilding programme team, colleagues from Forest Research and wider academia to learn from, identify synergies and efficiencies and share best practice across the Forest Wilding programme.
• Commission, manage and interpret surveys to gather baseline information relevant to wild area projects, including eDNA soil analysis, ecological and hydrological information.
• Undertake or commission feasibility studies to explore innovative approaches to secure nature recovery in wild areas

4. Communications and public engagement

• Lead the development and delivery of a stakeholder management plan and take the lead in building and managing relationships with relevant stakeholders.
• Work with district and national communications colleagues to develop and implement a communications plan.
• Where relevant, support the development of partnerships with neighbouring landowners to increase the scale and effectiveness of landscape scale nature recovery.
• Showcase the project to internal and external stakeholders to gain support for forest wilding, nature recovery and further delivery within the nation’s forests.

And any other tasks, reasonably requested by your line manager.

Person specification

Skills, knowledge & experience

Essential professional and technical experience

• A track record of successfully developing, managing and coordinating nature recovery projects.
• An experienced project manager, able to manage and prioritise workloads, meet deadlines and solve problems, and manage budgets
• Strong ecological knowledge, with practical experience of a range of land management interventions including in woodlands, heaths, wetlands, and uplands, relevant to the location of the role
• Experience of procurement and contract management, especially in the relevant areas of land management, feasibility studies and ecological survey and monitoring
• A great team worker, adept at working under your own initiative and as part of a multi-disciplinary team, taking ownership of the responsibilities of the role, building collaborative working relationships with colleagues, and being adaptable in the face of changing situations.
• Demonstrable skills in stakeholder management, with a track record of developing constructive collaborative relationships with a wide range of stakeholder groups, including public sector, private sector, and non-governmental organisations, volunteers and community groups.
• An excellent communicator, both written and verbally, able to adapt to a range of audiences.
• Competent using information technology, and sound knowledge of Microsoft Office suite, especially Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams.

Desirable professional and technical experience

• Sound experience in the forestry sector, operations and planning.
• Working knowledge of environmental legislation and designations, including their practical application. Qualifications

Essential

• Ecology or environmental degree, or equivalent professional experience in nature-focussed land management.
• A full and current driving licence that enables you to drive in the UK.

Desirable

As a senior commercial leader you will have real impact across the organisation, and within the Commercial team we are developing changes designed to make our approach to business agile, empowering our staff to reach their full potential.

This breadth of activity provides a multitude of opportunities for professional development and enables us to work across all industries from digital, global firsts in research and development, cutting edge innovation, through to traditional goods and services.

We pride ourselves on being inclusive and supportive, with a high team development and retention rate. At Navy Commercial, we believe in creating a safe, productive environment where everyone can thrive, with a well-defined set of team values that outlines our commitment to collaborative working.

The Navy Commercial team is already an influential, high-performing unit that works closely with our customers. We foster a culture of learning, committed to delivering the best results for operational delivery by embracing innovation, promoting an inclusive cultural environment and pushing the boundaries of commercial practices. The team are at the forefront within Defence of exploring how we can build AI into our working practices to streamline our work and ensure we can have our people focussed on the areas where human input has the greatest impact. By joining us you also gain access to the wider Defence Commercial function, with connections spanning the entire Civil Service commercial function.

We welcome fresh perspectives and ambition. If you're eager to shape the future and make a difference, we'd love to hear from you.

This role will take on a key role in the Navy Commercial Procure function; providing dedicated support to our customers in taking their concepts from early development through to contract supported by our team of dedicated commercial practitioners.

We are involved in procuring a hugely diverse array of services and equipment to support every facet of Navy delivery; items that aid the front line, core back-office delivery, and innovative technological developments that will drive future operations.

The Commercial Lead for Procure will be a member of the Navy Commercial Senior Leadership Team and will work closely with them to deliver the highest standard of Commercial support to the Navy. This post provides an excellent opportunity to build on your existing skill set across a number of commercial disciplines and with the support of the GCO to raise your profile and enable you to grow.

Experience of working in or with the public sector will be an advantage for the successful candidate but is not an essential criterion – we are looking for the right person with the right skill set, and the team come from a wide variety of backgrounds which creates a rich and diverse working environment. You will be responsible for a team of commercial leads in addition to working in a matrix approach across the wider Commercial function and with other stakeholders, providing senior leadership and guidance on tendering activities.

Locations

title: Digital Forensic Examiner III
description:
Benefits:
  • 401(k) matching
  • Competitive salary
  • Dental insurance
  • Health insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Vision insurance
  • Wellness resources
General Info:
Program Name: TRITON TO-03
Time Type: Full time
Job Posting Location: Springfield, VA
Clearance Required: TS/SCI w/CIP
Clearance Required to Start: TS/SCI

The CI Digital Forensic Examiner is tasked to produce, on average per annum, 48 weekly status reports and 12 final digital forensics reports, while providing expert support to CI Cyber Threat and Technical Analyst requirements.
Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
• Produce 48 weekly status reports and 12 final digital forensics reports, while providing expert support to CI Cyber Threat and Technical Analyst requirements.
• Perform Digital Media Acquisition and Digital Forensic Review of various platforms to include Windows, Linux, and Mac OS based systems using a variety of digital forensic tools.
• Investigate suspected instances of computer, mobile device, and network penetrations.
• Ingest media into an archive, copy media images, and employ advanced media forensics tools during a forensic examination (ENCASE and Windows Forensic Toolkit are two of the many tools used for media forensics).
• Investigate computer viruses and malicious code and prepare, write, and present reports and briefings.
• Provide weekly status updates when conducting forensics
• Provide a written report at the conclusion of each forensics examination. Reports will include, at a minimum, the following information (a template and standard operating procedures will be made available on site to provide additional guidance):
o Case File Number
o Computer Name
o User Name, File Names, etc…
o Background
o Investigation Details
o Status/Disposition
o Recommendations
• Intelligence Information Report (if deemed necessary by government lead)
o Case File Number
o Computer Name
o User Name
o Background
o Investigation Details
o Status/Disposition
• Personnel will support CI Incident Assessments to determine possible foreign intelligence entity involvement with an NGA computer system. In the process of supporting an Incident Assessment, reports must be produced and updated weekly. Reports will include, at a minimum, the following information (a template and standard operating procedures will be made available on site to provide additional guidance):
• Perform in-depth forensics examinations of computers, mobile devices, networks and other electronic and digital devices.
• Possess experience conducting computer forensics analysis within the Department of Defense and/or Intelligence Community.
• Attend periodic CI and law enforcement community cyber investigations awareness briefings.
• Brief CI cyber products and CI cyber service results to senior NGA leadership.
• Collaborate with internal and external Intelligence Community partners to share and gather technical threat information to enhance forensics examinations.
• Integrate information from forensics examinations and compile results into reports as required.
• Prepare and present forensic findings in the form of briefings and/or reports, to government leads and managers as required.
• Participate in Intelligence Community and Department of Defense technical exchange and collaboration meetings as required.
• Produce detailed CI cyber forensics reports as required.
• Provide support to all CI mission functions as required.
• Participate in IC Community and NGA technical meetings and working groups to address issues related to computer security and vulnerabilities.
• Investigate suspected instances of computer, mobile device, and network penetrations.
• Effectively utilize all applications and common analytic software tools (i.e., Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Analyst Notebook).
• Coordinate CI Cyber activities originating from Enterprise Incident Response Events.
• Conduct liaison between CI Office, Insider Threat, Cyber Security Operations Center (CSOC), and other NGA Offices as applicable to conducting the CI Cyber Mission
Minimum Qualifications:
• Shall possess a minimum of 7 years forensic experience in CI investigations
• Gain and maintain a digital forensic examiner certification within six months of assignment. Qualifying certification sources include government, military, and industry.
• Possess or obtain certification to comply with DoD 8570.01-M Information Assurance (IA) requirements within one calendar year of assignment. Shall possess or obtain and maintain IA III certification.
Desired Qualifications:
• Be a credentialed graduate of an accredited federal CI, federal law enforcement, DoD CI, or DoD Law Enforcement training academy (ex. FBI Academy).
• Possess a Bachelor’s degree in a Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics discipline.
• Possess and demonstrate knowledge and understanding of foreign adversaries’ security and intelligence services, terrorist organizations, and cyber threats posed to NGA, DoD, and IC partners.
• Possess a DoD Cyber Crimes Investigator certification.
• Experience with the latest forensic technologies such as Access Data Forensic Toolkit (FTK).
• Possess a digital forensic examiner certification. Qualifying certification sources include government, military, and industry.
• Possess ability to coach teammates to achieve objectives.
• Possess ability to monitor and track progress towards achievable measures.


Physical Requirements:
  • The person in this position must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time. Occasionally move about inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, or to communicate with co-workers, management, and customers, via email, phone, and or virtual communication, which may involve delivering presentations.

title: Principal Instructor
description:
SOTI is committed to providing its employees with endless possibilities; learning new things, working with the latest technologies and making a difference in the world.



SOTI does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process. You can verify the authenticity of any SOTI job opportunities by visiting SOTI Careers. SOTI shall not be liable for any fraudulent recruitment activities carried out by unauthorized individuals or organizations.



What You'll Do

  • Deliver practical and theoretical technical training sessions, taking an active and responsive mentoring role in developing and disseminating knowledge to internal and external technical global audiences, which may include partners, customers, and end users.
  • Build and maintain deep knowledge of the entire SOTI One Platform product portfolio, not limited to MobiControl and inclusive of other MDM/EMM platforms as applicable.
  • Deliver exceptional presentations, using advanced communication and interpersonal skills, exhibiting a high degree of professionalism as a representative of Global Training and SOTI.
  • Communicate with excellent command of the English language, in both writing and speech — this role regularly engages global stakeholders, produces documentation used across regions, and represents SOTI to international audiences, making clear, professional English communication essential, not optional.
  • Consistently demonstrate a positive attitude to ensure high-quality outputs, consistent delivery of commitments, and a rich learning experience for students.
  • Demonstrate the technical fluency to clearly explain complex technical terminology; not just execute a process, but describe each step's purpose, what fails if it's skipped, and how to walk through it without reading from a script.
  • Make sound decisions, remain agile and flexible, and exercise good judgment when circumstances don't go as expected.
  • Maintain solid awareness of the different contractual relationships between partners and SOTI, and the limitations/operational parameters governing what can be shared with each partner, to protect confidentiality and integrity.
  • Collaborate closely and proactively with Global Training team members — including regional peers and the India/APAC lead Principal Instructor — and take direction from the Manager of Principal Instructor Operations to create, manage, and deliver training plans for global and regional audiences.
  • Demonstrate flexibility to travel extensively across India and the broader APAC region to deliver Instructor-Led Training, and the ability to organize Web-Based Training and self-learning strategies where in-person delivery isn't practical.
  • Have flexibility with working hours, including starting later in the day where needed, to accommodate coordination and delivery across global time zones (APAC and EMEA) as required by the business.
  • Oversee training quality for locations not visited in person, by building strong working relationships with in-region personnel.
  • Act as a lead facilitator for training initiatives, ensuring world-class delivery and that the learner experience is never compromised — across a region spanning multiple languages, markets, and levels of technical maturity.
  • Bring an audience-focused facilitation approach, adapting delivery style and pacing to a wide range of technical backgrounds and English proficiency levels among learners.
  • Actively apply a continuous improvement process to close the loop on feedback, addressing trainer issues and negative comments with a solutions-first mindset.

Impact and Contribution

  • The candidate's role will encompass individual managing contributions, setting and maintaining standards, and ensuring others adhere to Global Training's policies, processes, and procedures to be considered eligible to deliver training.
  • Assess trainer readiness to deliver and facilitate training to a SOTI quality standard is critical to the credibility and overall success of our products and programs. Trainer authorization is a prerequisite to authenticating a SOTI trainer.
  • Trainer to be certified on SOTI product certifications and other applicable certifications important to understanding MDM & EMM environments and adjacent platforms.
  • SOTI Certified Trainer certification is maintained and recertified every 2 years in keeping with Global Training's evolving training techniques and digital learning standards.

Collaboration & Cross-Functional Teams

  • Act as an SME for product knowledge intake, contributing solutions and assisting the Content Manager with deliverables and materials, aligning needs with Programs and Project training plans.
  • Represent facilitation, working with product owners/managers to deliver training for new product introductions (NPI), including special events and training requests as supported by Global Training's business model/mandate.
  • Communicate proactively and in writing on status, blockers, and process changes — this is a collaborative team, not a set of independent operators, and visibility across the group is expected as a standard, not an exception.

Experience You'll Bring

  • Adult learning education background/post-secondary education equivalency.
  • Excellent written and spoken English communication skills — essential given the global, cross-regional nature of this role.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to work effectively across culturally and linguistically diverse audiences.
  • Exceptional presentation skills, proficient in MS Office Suite.
  • Very comfortable working, participating and communicating in a highly collaborative team environment.
  • Proven partner relationship management experience.
  • Strong knowledge and experience with MDM/EMM products and solutions.
  • Advanced knowledge of emergent technologies, Windows Modern management, and Apple products.
  • 3-5 years of related work portfolio experience.
  • Willingness and ability to travel extensively across India and the broader APAC region.

If you want to bring your ideas to life, apply at SOTI today.

title: Vice President, Program Management
description:
At Kailera, we are bold, authentic and committed to our mission of developing therapies that give people the power to transform their lives and elevate their overall health. Rooted in an entrepreneurial spirit and a team-oriented culture, we are working together to advance Kailera’s mission to advance novel therapies for obesity and related conditions.

We are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes collaboration, integrity, and excellence. As we expand, we seek the most talented individuals with diverse backgrounds, cultures, perspectives, and experiences to join our team.

What You’ll Do:

The Vice President, Program Management is accountable for the operational execution of Kailera’s development programs, with a strong emphasis on late-stage development. Reporting to the Chief Business and Operating Officer, this leader will serve as the day-to-day engine of the program management function – ensuring that integrated plans are built, maintained, and executed with rigor. The Vice President will directly manage a team of thee Program Managers (plus additional contract Program Managers) and serve as the cross-functional connective tissue that keeps teams aligned, milestones on track, and risks visible.

This role demands a leader who is equally comfortable driving detailed execution and operating at the strategic level alongside functional heads and senior leadership. The ideal candidate brings deep Phase 3 experience, strong team development instincts, and the discipline to build and sustain operational infrastructure in a fast-moving organization.

Required location: Waltham, MA (hub-based, onsite 3-4 days per week)

Responsibilities:

  • Own integrated program management across Kailera's development portfolio across all programs, with primary accountability for Phase 3 programs
  • Drive the evolution of Kailera’s program management capabilities toward a portfolio-based framework, providing enterprise-wide visibility into milestones, dependencies, resources, risks, and strategic priorities
  • Build and maintain comprehensive integrated project plans, timelines, and cross-functional dependencies
  • Track and communicate program status, key milestones, critical path activities, and risks with clarity and consistency
  • Ensure cross-functional teams are aligned on priorities, deliverables, and decision points at all stages of development
  • Proactively identify risks and interdependencies; drive issue resolution with urgency and accountability
  • Participate in Quarterly Business Reviews, providing program updates, highlighting key milestones, risks, and strategic considerations across the portfolio
  • Partner closely with Clinical, Regulatory, CMC, and Medical Affairs to ensure Phase 3 plans are fully integrated and execution-ready
  • Manage program timelines from Phase 3 initiation through NDA submission readiness, coordinating across all workstreams
  • Ensure submission-enabling activities – data management, regulatory strategy, CMC milestones – are tracked as integrated components of the program plan
  • Support the COO in shaping late-stage development strategy by providing operational perspective and risk intelligence
  • Directly manage, mentor, and develop a team of three Program Managers and additional contractors, supporting cross-functional program teams
  • Build a high-performing, accountable team culture with clear expectations, strong communication norms, and a commitment to continuous improvement
  • Serve as a model for cross-functional collaboration and operational excellence across the organization
  • Support the professional growth of each PM through coaching, feedback, and expanding scope of responsibility over time
  • Emulate Kailera’s culture and reinforce Operating Principles, ensuring that both program outcomes and the behaviors used to achieve them reflect the company’s commitment to collaboration, accountability, transparency, and operational excellence
  • Design and maintain program governance frameworks, review cadences, and reporting structures in alignment with the COO
  • Build a world class program management office capability – develop and standardize templates, dashboards, and tools that drive efficiency and visibility across programs; this includes a communication discipline working with the program teams and helping to integrate across the key internal forums
  • Ensure program documentation – integrated development plans, target product profiles, risk registers – is current, accurate, and decision-ready
  • Drive meeting conduct, decision-making discipline, and lessons-learned processes with a focus on operational excellence
  • Serve as a trusted partner and day-to-day interface for functional leads across Clinical, Regulatory, CMC, Commercial, and Finance
  • Prepare and present program updates, milestone summaries, and risk assessments for senior leadership and governance forums
  • Operate with influence rather than authority – building alignment and driving accountability across a matrixed organization
  • Support the COO in representing the program management function at the executive level and in board-level discussions
  • Collaborate with Program Leader / SVP Franchise Lead to align strategic objectives with execution plans, ensuring program teams remain focused on priorities, milestones, risks, and decision points
  • Ensure all program activities comply with applicable regulations, ICH guidelines, and company policies
  • Champion data-driven, transparent decision-making, and ethical business practices across the program portfolio
  • Maintain robust risk management oversight and escalation protocols

Required Qualifications:

  • 15+ years of progressive experience in biotech or pharma, with a strong focus on program management in clinical-stage organizations
  • Demonstrated track record of driving Phase 3 programs with rigor – ideally through NDA submission – in both pharma and biotech settings
  • Direct people management experience required; proven ability to build and develop high-performing PM teams
  • Deep operational knowledge of integrated development planning, cross-functional execution, and governance infrastructure
  • Experience in general medicine therapeutic areas (metabolic disease, cardiovascular, endocrinology, or similar) preferred; oncology-only backgrounds are less preferred
  • History of succeeding in lean, fast-moving biotech environments – bringing structure and discipline without sacrificing speed
  • Exceptional communication and facilitation skills; ability to distill complexity and drive clarity at all levels of the organization

Education:

  • Advanced degree (MBA, MS, PhD, PharmD, or equivalent) preferred
Salary Range
$272,000—$340,000 USD

For Full Time Roles: This range represents the company’s good-faith estimate of the salary at the time of posting. Actual pay may vary based on experience, skills, qualifications, location, and internal equity. We also offer comprehensive health coverage, flexible time off, paid holidays, and a year-end shutdown. Enjoy a monthly wellness stipend, generous 401(k) match, tuition reimbursement, commuter benefits, disability and life insurance, plus annual bonus opportunities and equity grants—because your well-being and future matter to us.

Kailera Therapeutics, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer that does not discriminate on the basis of actual or perceived race (including traits historically associated with race, such as hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, creed, religion (including religious dress and grooming practices), national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, age (40 and over), sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, pregnancy-related conditions, and lactation), gender identity or expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital status, military service and veteran status, physical or mental disability, genetic information, reproductive health decisions, domestic victim status, political affiliation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws and ordinances.

title: SR Specialist, Planner Scheduler Maintenance & Calibration
description:
37735877, Senior Maintenance Planner / Scheduler

Location: Fremont, CA 94555
Job Type: Contract – Approximately 9 Months
Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM
Work Arrangement: 100% Onsite
Industry: Pharmaceutical / Biotechnology Manufacturing

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced Senior Maintenance Planner / Scheduler to support maintenance operations at a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in Fremont, CA. This position is responsible for planning, scheduling, and coordinating preventive and corrective maintenance activities to maximize equipment reliability, minimize production downtime, and ensure efficient utilization of maintenance resources.

The ideal candidate will have a strong background in industrial maintenance planning, experience with Computerized Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS), and the ability to coordinate activities across maintenance, engineering, production, and external contractors.

Key Responsibilities

  • Plan, schedule, and coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance activities within a manufacturing environment.
  • Develop detailed maintenance work plans, including labor estimates, required materials, equipment, tools, and safety requirements.
  • Coordinate maintenance schedules with production, engineering, maintenance personnel, and contractors to minimize operational disruptions.
  • Create, update, and manage maintenance work orders within CMMS systems.
  • Ensure necessary spare parts, MRO materials, tools, and equipment are available before scheduled maintenance activities.
  • Review equipment maintenance histories, identify recurring failures, and recommend improvements to maintenance programs.
  • Monitor maintenance performance, analyze work order completion data, and develop KPI reports.
  • Coordinate procurement of maintenance materials, outside services, and contractor support.
  • Support preventive maintenance program improvements and equipment reliability initiatives.
  • Maintain accurate maintenance documentation, equipment records, and inventory information.
  • Ensure maintenance planning activities comply with established safety procedures and company policies.
  • Publish weekly maintenance schedules and coordinate priorities with relevant departments.

Required Qualifications

  • Associate's degree in Engineering, Maintenance, Industrial Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Minimum of 4 years of experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
  • Demonstrated experience in maintenance planning, scheduling, and work order management.
  • Experience working with CMMS software and preventive maintenance programs.
  • Working knowledge of ERP systems such as SAP or Oracle.
  • Understanding of industrial equipment maintenance, repair procedures, and maintenance resource planning.
  • Experience coordinating maintenance personnel, contractors, materials, and equipment.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or other regulated manufacturing environments.
  • Experience with SAP, Oracle, IBM Maximo, or COMOS.
  • Knowledge of maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) inventory management.
  • Experience developing maintenance KPIs and analyzing equipment downtime.
  • Familiarity with preventive maintenance optimization and equipment reliability programs.
  • Experience coordinating maintenance activities requiring specialized permits, tools

title: Robotics Engineer - Mechanical Design and Integration
description:
Job Summary

Join EIT’s AutoLabs team to design, build, and deploy robotic systems that automate scientific work. This is a hands-on role focused on mechanical design and integration, working across electrical systems, software, and control. You will bring these disciplines together to turn scientific requirements and working prototypes into reliable, maintainable machines used in laboratories.

The role requires a strong systems engineering approach: understanding how the complete machine should behave, managing dependencies between subsystems, and verifying performance at system level. You will work with automation scientists and specialist engineers from requirements and concept development through build, commissioning, and operational use.

You will use iterative hardware development practices to test assumptions early, improve designs through practical evidence, and productionise prototypes while maintaining appropriate safety and configuration controls.

We welcome engineers with applied, deployment, or product development experience in industrial automation, robotics, manufacturing, instrumentation, or related fields. Previous laboratory automation experience is valuable but is not essential.

You will be required to work in Oxford 4 days a week for this role.

Requirements

Key Responsibilities

  • Translate scientific workflows and user needs into system requirements, operating concepts, interfaces, and measurable acceptance criteria.
  • Develop integrated robotic and automation system concepts, evaluating trade-offs across mechanical, electrical, software, control, safety, and operational needs.
  • Design and develop mechanisms, end-effectors, fixtures, motion assemblies, and machine structures, considering manufacture, assembly, cleaning, and servicing.
  • Specify and mechanically integrate sensors, actuators, drives, and control hardware, working with electrical and controls specialists on wiring and interfaces.
  • Adapt robot programs and control sequences to support mechanical integration and testing, working with software and controls specialists on equipment coordination, sensing, and fault recovery.
  • Plan iterative hardware development through focused prototypes, staged integration, design reviews, and short build–test–learn cycles.
  • Maintain system interfaces, design baselines, and configuration records so hardware and software changes remain compatible and traceable.
  • Assemble, commission, calibrate, and troubleshoot complete systems in the workshop and at deployment sites, resolving integration issues under operational conditions.
  • Contribute to machinery risk assessments and hazard reviews, translating findings into design measures, guarding, interlocks, and safe operating and maintenance arrangements.
  • Plan and carry out verification and validation, covering performance, reliability, foreseeable misuse, fault conditions, and recovery from interrupted operation.
  • Productionise prototypes and support deployment, working with scientists, technicians, and suppliers to improve usability, repeatability, and maintainability.

Essential Knowledge, Skills, and Experience

  • Degree or equivalent practical experience in Robotics, Mechatronics, Mechanical, Electrical/Electronic, Control, or a related engineering discipline.
  • Experience delivering integrated robotic, automated, or electromechanical systems through build, on-site commissioning, deployment, and troubleshooting in operational environments.
  • Practical systems engineering experience, including requirements capture, functional decomposition, interface definition, trade studies, and system-level verification and validation.
  • Strong mechanical design capability, with practical understanding of electrical integration, software, and controls.
  • Experience applying agile or iterative hardware development practices, using prototypes and test evidence to reduce uncertainty and guide design decisions.
  • Experience managing changes across interconnected hardware and software, including configuration control and assessment of system-wide effects.
  • Experience designing mechanical assemblies using 3D CAD and producing engineering drawings for manufacture and assembly, with the ability to interpret electrical schematics.
  • Ability to develop or modify automation software and control logic using relevant tools, such as Python, C++, PLC programming, or robot programming environments.
  • Practical understanding of machinery hazards, risk assessment, and safe design principles, including the distinction between operational software controls and safety-related functions.
  • Systematic fault-finding skills and experience testing complete systems against defined requirements.
  • Ability to collaborate with scientists, users, and specialist engineers and communicate engineering decisions clearly.

Desirable Knowledge, Skills, and Experience

  • Experience productionising prototypes or developing machines for sustained operational use.
  • Experience with industrial or collaborative robots, custom tooling, precision handling, or multi-axis motion systems.
  • Experience contributing to machinery safety assessments, safety-related control design, or conformity assessment with competent specialists.
  • Familiarity with failure analysis techniques such as FMEA and their use in design and test planning.
  • Experience with design for manufacture and assembly, component sourcing, and supplier coordination.
  • Familiarity with communications middleware and industrial protocols connecting equipment, controllers, and automation software.
  • Experience with machine vision, calibration, simulation, or automated system testing.
  • Experience with modular automation or laboratory processes requiring controlled handling and cleaning.

Key Attributes

  • Thinks about the complete system and takes ownership of how its parts work together.
  • Practical and resourceful, moving comfortably between design, programming, assembly, and commissioning.
  • Balances rapid iteration with safety, engineering discipline, and dependable operation.
  • Uses test evidence to make decisions and challenge assumptions.
  • Collaborative, curious, and attentive to the needs of scientists, operators, and maintainers.

Benefits

We offer the following salary and benefits:

Enhanced holiday pay

Pension

Life Assurance

Income Protection

Private Medical Insurance

Hospital Cash Plan

Therapy Services

Perk Box

Electric Car Scheme

--

At the Ellison Institute, we believe a collaborative, inclusive team is key to our success. We are building a supportive environment where creative risks are encouraged, and everyone feels heard. Valuing emotional intelligence, empathy, respect, and resilience, we encourage people to be curious and to have a shared commitment to excellence. Join us and make an impact!

title: Business Intelligence Manager
description:
We’re looking for a Business Intelligence Manager to turn market, customer, competitor and performance data into commercial intelligence, to improve the commercial decisions across all three brands: Cookie Information, Piwik PRO, and Sheltr. This role reports to the Director of Revenue Operations (RevOps).


We are open to on-site, hybrid, and remote working within two time zones of our offices (CET).



About Us

Our group brings together three European software brands that help organisations earn and use data with trust: Cookie Information for consent management; Piwik PRO for privacy-by-design analytics and data activation; and Sheltr for reliably finding personal data in internal data sources.


Headquartered in Copenhagen with an office in Wrocław, our team of 180 people have been building trusted data solutions since 2011. We work with companies and marketing teams across various industries that take control of their data model, including some of the most data-sensitive clients in healthcare, finance, energy & utilities, and the public sector. We are proud that our clients rely on us to meet GDPR and EU data residency requirements across EMEA and the US, as this regulatory depth is hard to build and replicate. We believe compliance and performance are not opposites. Consented data, auditable analytics and full visibility of personal data belong to one data journey; together they form a foundation that marketing, IT, legal and the C-level can rely on.


Our journey is to move from a regulation-driven house of brands to one unified company with a clear point of view. We are creating a new category around this complete data journey, and together we are building an enterprise-ready, data-driven revenue engine led by thought leadership. Want to join us on this journey? Keep reading to find out how you can help shape this with us.



The Role

In this role, you will play a key part in driving business growth across Cookie Information, Piwik PRO, and Sheltr by turning internal performance metrics, customer insights, and market trends into actionable strategic guidance for leadership.


Your key responsibilities will include:

  • Identifying revenue opportunities, diagnose funnel/segment performance gaps, and quantify business impact.
  • Synthesising internal data, win/loss research, and 1–3 year competitor/market trends to deliver strategic recommendations.
  • Building and own commercial dashboards across sales, marketing, and revenue funnels.
  • Partnering with data, marketing, and AI teams to maintain robust tracking, data models, and data warehouse extraction.
  • Leveraging AI-enabled analytics paired with rigorous human validation to support executive planning cycles.



About You
You’re an experienced Business Intelligence Manager with an analytical and commercial mindset. You extract and connect data quickly.


You bring:

  • Commercial and revenue intelligence.
  • B2B SaaS funnel & metrics acumen: pipeline, conversion, CAC, CLV, churn.
  • Dashboarding & data architecture experience, incl. data integration.
  • Market & customer research, incl. competitor analysis.
  • Turning data into opportunities and recommendations, not just reports.
  • Stakeholder management: executives, vendors, agencies.
  • Looker Studio / Data Studio, Tableau, HubSpot.
  • Proven record of insight-led recommendations with commercial impact.
  • AI & automation acumen.
  • Fluency in English (C2).


Nice-to-haves:

  • Privacy, consent or analytics market knowledge.
  • Multi-brand / multi-market environment exposure.
  • Experience commissioning research agencies.
  • Knowledge of Python.



What we offer

  • The opportunity for you to shape the future growth of the company.
  • An interesting mix of internal data, market and customer research.
  • AI-first analytics with a real freedom to build.
  • Professional development budget, health insurance, and other benefits.
  • A positive, informal workplace.



Application process
We’re looking to fill the position as soon as possible and will be inviting candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis, so don’t hesitate to send your application today.


This is what our recruitment process looks like:

  • A brief screening call with our Talent Partner (online, approx. 30 mins)
  • An in-depth interview with the hiring manager and a member of the team (online)
  • A final interview with the hiring manager, including a live case (online)



Our Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

At Cookie Information & Piwik PRO we value diversity as a cornerstone of our success. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, religion, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability. We recognise that certain groups are underrepresented in the tech industry, and we encourage everyone to apply and help us shape a more inclusive workspace.

title: Operating Model Lead
location: Bristol, Cardiff, Edinburgh, Liverpool, Manchester, Leeds, Telford - Parkside Court, Stratford. Please note that due to workforce controls, Liverpool is only available to existing HMRC staff in this location.
description:
• Job grade: Grade 6
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: HMRC - CDIO - Finance, Portfolio, Performance, and Organisational Transformation
  • Type of role: Human Resources
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Bristol, Cardiff, Edinburgh, Liverpool, Manchester, Leeds, Telford - Parkside Court, Stratford.
Please note that due to workforce controls, Liverpool is only available to existing HMRC staff in this location.

About the job

Job summary

Discover a career in your hands at HMRC. Whether you're seeking purpose, growth, or a workplace that gives you a true sense of belonging, hear from some of our employees as they share their story about what it’s really like to work at HMRC.

Visit our YouTube channel to watch the full series and come and discover your potential.

As an Operating Model Lead, you will provide strategic leadership for the design, evolution and continuous improvement of HMRC's Chief Digital and Information Office (CDIO) operating model. You will act as the strategic owner of the CDIO operating model, setting its direction, overseeing its continuous evolution, and leading the portfolio of improvement activity and people required to ensure it remains effective, sustainable and aligned to organisational priorities.

You will lead a team of Operating Model Managers, acting as the senior internal consulting lead for operating model transformation across CDIO. You will shape the long-term direction of how CDIO delivers value through technology services, digital products and platforms, ensuring operating model decisions support organisational objectives, improve delivery performance and enable successful business outcomes.

CDIO is moving to a Products and Platform-based organisation, with value delivered through Value Streams and a standard process framework. In this role, you will lead the operating model agenda that makes this shift successful and sustainable. You will work with senior leaders to define the future operating model, align strategic priorities, shape organisational design and governance, and ensure operating model improvements are implemented consistently across CDIO.

This role suits someone who combines strategic thinking with strong delivery leadership. You will lead a team who use evidence, insight and organisational data to identify systemic barriers to effective delivery and organisational performance, setting priorities for improvement across governance, operating rhythms, organisational design, decision-making, ways of working, tooling, culture, people and supply chain.

You will also lead the measures, frameworks and governance required to assess operating model effectiveness and demonstrate improvements in organisational performance, value delivery and strategic outcomes.

Job description

At this level, you will lead the strategic direction and continuous evolution of the CDIO operating model. You will oversee a portfolio of operating model initiatives and provide leadership across operational and strategic priorities, ensuring CDIO has the structures, governance and capabilities required to deliver value effectively.

You will work closely with senior leaders across CDIO and HMRC to identify opportunities for organisational improvement, shape strategic decisions and ensure the operating model continues to evolve in response to business needs, technology change and organisational priorities.

You will provide leadership to Operating Model Managers, ensuring interventions are aligned to a coherent operating model strategy and deliver measurable outcomes.

Person specification

Your responsibilities will typically include:

  • Define operating model strategy: Develop and maintain the strategic vision, principles and roadmap for the CDIO operating model, ensuring alignment with organisational objectives, product and platform transformation, and future business needs.
  • Shape organisational effectiveness: Identify systemic opportunities and risks affecting organisational performance, developing operating model interventions that improve governance, accountability, decision-making, prioritisation and value delivery.
  • Lead operating model transformation: Oversee a portfolio of operating model improvement initiatives, ensuring work is focused on the highest-value opportunities and delivers sustainable organisational change.
  • Influence senior decision-making: Work with senior leaders to build consensus on complex and potentially contentious issues, providing evidence-based recommendations and securing commitment for change.
  • Establish governance and performance frameworks: Define and continuously improve the governance, measures and operating rhythms required to assess organisational health, operating model maturity and value delivery performance.
  • Build organisational capability: Develop operating model capability across CDIO through coaching, thought leadership, standards, frameworks, communities of practice and repeatable approaches to continuous improvement.
  • Lead and develop people: Provide leadership, coaching and direction to Operating Model Managers, creating a high-performing team capable of delivering complex operating model interventions across CDIO.
  • Evidence value and impact: Establish meaningful measures and reporting that demonstrate the effectiveness of operating model changes, including organisational performance, delivery flow, value realisation, decision quality and strategic outcomes.
Essential criteria
  • Significant experience owning and evolving an organisation-wide operating model, establishing strategic direction, prioritising and leading a portfolio of operating model improvements.
  • Significant experience leading large-scale operating model transformation initiatives in complex organisations, with evidence of delivering sustainable organisational outcomes through direct leadership and leadership through others.
  • Experience defining operating model strategy and translating organisational objectives into practical operating model improvements across governance, structures, processes, roles, ways of working and performance management.
  • Experience working with senior executives to shape organisational direction, influence strategic decisions and build alignment across multiple stakeholder groups with competing priorities.
  • Experience using evidence, organisational data and insight to identify systemic issues, inform strategic decisions and assess the effectiveness of operating model interventions.
  • Strong leadership skills, with experience leading, developing and coaching multidisciplinary teams whilst creating a culture of continuous improvement and accountability.
  • Experience applying systems thinking and organisational design principles to understand complex challenges and design effective interventions that improve organisational performance.
  • Experience operating successfully in large, complex organisations, navigating ambiguity, competing demands and significant organisational change.
Desirable criteria
  • Experience leading operating model, organisational effectiveness or transformation functions within a technology, digital or product-led organisation.
  • Experience working in a consultancy or internal consulting environment, providing strategic advice and delivery leadership across multiple concurrent engagements.
  • Experience establishing organisational performance frameworks, maturity models or value measurement approaches to support executive decision-making.

Further Location Information

Please ensure that you only apply for a location that you are willing and able to work from, as we will only make one offer of employment. Any additional notes included in a ‘Further Location Preferences (optional)’ field within the application form, will not be considered. Please be aware that you cannot change your location preference after submitting your application.

Leeds Locations

Moves Adjustment Payment will be available for this role, provided the successful applicant is a current HMRC colleague in Bradford and meets the eligibility requirements outlined in the HMRC’s Moves Adjustment Payment guidance.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £71,725, HM Revenue and Customs contributes £20,778 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

HMRC operates both Flexible and Hybrid Working policies, allowing you to balance your work and personal commitments. We welcome applications from those who need to work a more flexible arrangement and will agree to requests where possible, considering our operational and customer service needs.

We offer a generous leave allowance, starting at 25 days and increasing by a day for every year of qualifying service up to a maximum of 30 days.

  • Pension - We make contributions to our colleagues’ Alpha pension equal to at least 28.97% of their salary.
  • Family friendly policies.
  • Personal support.
  • Coaching and development.

To find out more about HMRC benefits and find out what it’s really like to work for HMRC hear from our insiders or visit Thinking of joining the Civil Service

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Strengths and Experience.

How to Apply

As part of the application process, you will be asked to provide the following:

  • A name-blind CV including your Job History up to your last 5 roles (100 words per role), giving a brief summary of your skills and experience, what you delivered and any key achievements in each role.

  • A 750-word Personal Statement. Your Personal Statement should tell us about a time when you defined and led a strategic operating model transformation within a complex digital, technology, product or platform-based organisation. Explain how you translated organisational priorities into a clear operating model vision, principles and roadmap; identified and prioritised systemic opportunities for improvement; built alignment among senior leaders with competing priorities; and led a portfolio of changes through others. Describe how you ensured the transformation was embedded and sustainable, and how you measured its impact on organisational performance, value delivery and strategic outcomes.

Please complete a separate statement (Max 250 words) for the Desirable Criteria where applicable. This is not mandatory for the role but may be considered by the vacancy-holder where candidates have the same scores at interview.

Further details around what this will entail are listed on the application form.

Sift

In the event of a large number of applications being received, an initial sift may be held on the Personal Statement.

At full sift your CV and Personal Statement will be assessed, with the successful candidates being invited to interview.

We may also raise the score required at any stage of the process if we receive a high number of applications.

Interview

During the panel interview you will be asked experienced based questions and there will be further questions in relation to the Personal Statement.

You will also be asked strength-based questions to also explore what you enjoy and your motivations relevant to the job role.

This is an example of a strengths-based question:

“It is often said that the customer's needs should come first. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?”

There is no expectation or requirement for you to prepare for the strengths-based questions in advance of the interview, though you may find it helpful to spend some time reflecting on what you enjoy doing and what you do well.

Interviews will take place via video link. Sift and Interview dates to be confirmed.

Please note that circumstances may arise that require the planned interview format to change. We will endeavour to provide you with as much notice of any change as possible.

Eligibility

Please take extra care to tick the correct boxes in the eligibility sections of your application form. Mistakes sometimes happen but if you contact us later than two working days (Monday-Friday) before the vacancy closes, we may not be able to reopen your application for you. If you do make a mistake with your eligibility form or have withdrawn yourself in error and need your application reinstated whilst the campaign is still live, please contact us via: unitybusinessservicesrecruitmentresults@hmrc.gov.uk – Use the subject line to insert appropriate wording for example – ‘Please re-open my application – [insert vacancy ref] & vacancy closing date [insert date]’.

To check that you are eligible to apply for this role, please review the eligibility information before submitting your application.

Exceptionally, candidates who are not successful at this grade may be considered for appointment to similar roles at a lower grade where the eligibility criteria are met. If this applies, we will contact you directly.

The HMRC app can help you with your application

The HMRC app can provide you with your past 5 years' employment history, making the process of filling in your application quicker and easier.

If successful in your application, you will need your National Insurance number for the onboarding process.

Download the HMRC app now and save your National Insurance number to your digital phone wallet.

How to download the HMRC app and sign up for an account

Download the free HMRC app from the App Store or Google Play store.

If you have an HMRC online account already, sign straight in using your ID and password. If not, you can prove your identity by answering some questions or providing your photo ID.

You’ll then be able to access the app quickly and easily by signing in using a 6-digit PIN, your fingerprint, or facial recognition.

You can find guidance for technical issues on GOV.UK: Technical support with HMRC online services.

Reserve List

A reserve list may be held for up to 12 months from which further appointments may be made for the same or similar roles – if this applies to you, we’ll let you know via your Civil Service Jobs account.

Merit List

After interview, a single merit list will be created, and you will only be considered for posts in locations you have expressed a preference for. Appointments will be made in strict merit order in line with the set number of roles in each location.

Criminal Record Check

Applications received from candidates with a criminal record are considered fairly in accordance with the DBS Code of Practice and the Recruitment of ex-offenders Policy.

Hybrid working at HMRC

HMRC is an office-based organisation, and colleagues are expected to spend 60% of their working time in the office. Our offices provide opportunity for interaction, collaboration which aids learning and development and a sense of community. Where the role allows it, and where the home environment is suitable, colleagues can work from home for up to 2 days a week, averaged over a calendar month (or a proportionate amount of time for colleagues who work less than full time).

Reasonable Adjustments

We want to make sure no one is put at a disadvantage during our recruitment process. To assist you with this, we will reduce or remove any barriers where possible and provide additional support where appropriate.

If you need a change to be made so that you can make your application, you should:

  • Contact the UBS Recruitment team via unitybusinessservicesrecruitmentresults@hmrc.gov.uk as soon as possible before the closing date to discuss your needs.

Complete the “Assistance required” section in the “Additional requirements” page of your application form to tell us what changes or help you might need further on in the recruitment process. For instance, you may need wheelchair access at interview, or if you’re deaf, a Language Service Professional.

Technical Support

If you are experiencing problems that cannot be resolved by our ‘help’ section, then technical support is available. You will receive a reply in 2 working days.

Important information for existing HMRC contractual homeworkers:

This role may be suitable for existing HMRC employees who are contractual homeworkers. Occasional attendance to the office will be required where there is a business need. Please consider the advertised office locations for this role when applying and only select locations from the ‘location preferences’ section that you can travel to.

Terms and Conditions

Customer facing roles in HMRC require the ability to converse at ease with members of the public and provide advice in accurate spoken English and/or Welsh where required. Where this is an essential requirement, this will be tested as part of the selection process.

HMRC has a presence in every region of the UK. For more information on where you might be working, review this information on our locations.

The Civil Service values honesty and integrity and expects all candidates to abide by these principles. The evidence you provide in your application must relate to your own experiences.

Any instances of plagiarism or other forms of cheating will be investigated and, if proven, the relevant application(s) will be withdrawn from the process.

Recording of interviews is prohibited unless explicit agreement is sought in line with the UK General Data Protection Regulations.

Questions relating to an individual application must be emailed as detailed later in this advert.

Applicants who are successful at interview will be, as part of pre-employment screening, subject to a check on the Internal Fraud Database (IFD). This check will provide information about employees who have been dismissed for fraud or dishonesty offences. title: Specialist - Spend Analytics
description:
Role: Specialist - Spend Analytics

Location: Gurgaon

Full/ Part-time: Full Time

Build a career with confidence

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions is committed to creating solutions that matter for people and our planet for generations to come. From the beginning, we've led in inventing new technologies and entirely new industries. Today, we continue to lead because we have a world-class, diverse workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do.

About the role

The Specialist – Spend Analytics will be responsible for transforming procurement spend data into actionable cost intelligence to drive insights and strategic decision-making related to procurement and cost optimization, generating actionable intelligence for the Global and Regional supply chain teams to achieve financial goals and improve overall operational efficiency. The role combines rigorous spend analytics with deep should-cost expertise — leveraging tools such as aPriori to build fact-based cost models that challenge supplier pricing, identify savings opportunities, and support high-stakes negotiations. A working knowledge of AI and machine learning techniques for spend analytics, anomaly detection, and pattern recognition will be a strong advantage, enabling the specialist to continuously elevate the analytical maturity of the COE and deliver commercially impactful outcomes at scale.

Key Responsibilities:

A. Spend Data Analysis & Interpretation

  • Conduct in-depth analysis of spend data to identify trends, patterns, and anomalies across categories and suppliers.
  • Utilize statistical techniques and data visualization tools to transform complex datasets into clear, meaningful insights for stakeholders.
  • Leverage tools such as Python, R, VBA, and advanced Excel to build scalable analytical workflows and automate repetitive data processing tasks.
  • Apply machine learning techniques to enhance spend classification, outlier detection, and predictive analytics capabilities.
  • Increase automation across key steps of the spend analysis lifecycle to improve speed, accuracy, and consistency of outputs.
  • Deliver robust, audit-ready spend analysis that supports strategic sourcing decisions at both global and regional levels.

B. Should Costing & Cost Intelligence

  • Build and validate detailed should-cost models for Build to Print categories including plastics, Sheet Metal, pressure die cast (PDC) components, machining, leveraging knowledge of raw materials, manufacturing processes, and cost drivers.
  • Maintain and continuously refine cost models using aPriori or equivalent tools to reflect current market dynamics and input cost movements.
  • Drive cost reduction initiatives through value engineering, design-to-cost analysis, and supplier negotiations.
  • Partner with engineering and commodity teams to apply should-cost outputs to RFQ benchmarking and fact-based negotiation preparation.

C. Market Intelligence & Sourcing Strategy

  • Monitor global market trends, raw material indices, supplier landscapes, and technological developments in the HVAC and related industries.
  • Leverage market intelligence to inform sourcing strategies, risk mitigation plans, and cost management decisions.
  • Identify alternative suppliers, emerging markets, and innovative manufacturing processes to enhance competitiveness.

D. Negotiation Preparation

  • Prepare structured negotiation packs for category managers, including should-cost breakdowns, market benchmarks, supplier scorecards, and price-volume analyses.
  • Conduct supplier cost walk-throughs and price justification reviews to equip sourcing teams with robust challenge frameworks.
  • Model negotiation scenarios and sensitivity analyses, including the impact of raw material price movements on target pricing.
  • Track negotiation outcomes and feed results back into cost models and spend databases to improve future analytical cycles.

E. Implementation & Value Capture

  • Drive or support the execution of initiatives generated from spend analytics, converting insights into real, measurable savings.
  • Ensure consistent tracking and reporting of value capture against identified savings pipeline.

F. Stakeholder Collaboration

  • Collaborate with stakeholders across the organisation — supply chain, engineering, operations, and quality — to understand spend analysis requirements and translate them into actionable insights.
  • Present findings, opportunity assessments, and recommendations in a clear and compelling manner to senior leadership.
  • Provide guidance and support in interpreting spend analytics findings and implementing recommendations across functions.
  • Facilitate cross-functional workshops to align on category strategies, savings priorities, and data quality improvement plans.

G. Continuous Improvement & Governance

  • Drive process improvements in sourcing, RFQ management, cost analysis, and spend reporting cycles.
  • Ensure compliance with procurement policies, contracts, and ethical sourcing standards.
  • Support digitalization and analytics initiatives, including deployment of BI platforms and AI-driven spend intelligence tools, to enhance sourcing effectiveness.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree from an accredited institution in Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, Data Science, or a related discipline.
  • 8+ years of experience in spend analytics, strategic sourcing, or cost engineering within a manufacturing or industrial procurement environment.
  • Strong understanding of part cost structures, manufacturing processes, and tooling across key direct spend categories.
  • Hands-on experience with aPriori or similar should-cost software is mandatory.
  • Experience with BI and data visualization tools (Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent).
  • Familiarity with AI/ML techniques applied to procurement analytics is a strong plus.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) for analytics and presentations is mandatory.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, along with strong interpersonal abilities for stakeholder management.
  • High learning agility, accountability, and effective collaboration skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in a global environment with stakeholders located in different regions.
  • Strong attention to detail with sharp observational skills to identify issues accurately and articulate findings effectively.

Benefits

We are committed to offering competitive benefits programs for all of our employees and enhancing our programs when necessary.

  • Have peace of mind and body with our health insurance
  • Drive forward your career through professional development opportunities
  • Achieve your personal goals with our Employee Assistance Programme

Our commitment to you

Our greatest assets are the expertise, creativity and passion of our employees. We strive to provide a great place to work that attracts, develops and retains the best talent, promotes employee engagement, fosters teamwork and ultimately drives innovation for the benefit of our customers. We strive to create an environment where you feel that you belong, with diversity and inclusion as the engine to growth and innovation. We develop and deploy best-in-class programs and practices, providing enriching career opportunities, listening to employee feedback and always challenging ourselves to do better. This is The Carrier Way.

Join us and make a difference.

Apply Now!

title: FPV Pilot – Acro Line-of-Sight Specialist, DoorDash Air
description:
About the Team

DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We explore robotics and automation to transform last-mile logistics in the long term. If you have a passion for applying autonomous aviation technologies in a service used by millions of people, then we want to talk to you!

About the Role

We are seeking a highly skilled FPV Pilot with advanced acro mode flight experience for visual line-of-sight operations (no goggles). This role focuses on hands-on drone testing and evaluation to support the development of next-generation UAS technologies. You’ll work closely with systems and flight engineers to provide actionable flight data and feedback that drive design improvements and system reliability.

This position is fully on-site at our Bay Point, California test facility. Work hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will...

  • Operate small and mid-size multi-rotor and fixed-wing UAS platforms in acro mode within visual line of sight (VLOS) environments.
  • Conduct test flights, calibration routines, and performance evaluations under engineering supervision.
  • Collaborate closely with systems engineers to provide high-quality, data-driven feedback on flight performance, controls tuning, and system reliability.
  • Maintain detailed logs of flight hours, aircraft condition, and observed anomalies.
  • Support safety and compliance processes in accordance with FAA Part 107 and internal operating procedures.
  • Participate in system validation efforts involving PX4, ArduPilot, Auterion, and Herelink control systems.
  • Contribute to iterative design reviews, prototype evaluations, and test readiness reviews.

We’re excited about you because you have...

  • FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate (required; will be verified).
  • 100+ hours of logged FPV flight time.
  • 1+ year of consistent acro mode flight experience under visual line of sight (no goggles).
  • Demonstrated experience with multi-rotor UAS operations (required).
  • Proven FPV flying background and ability to demonstrate control precision in manual (acro) mode.
  • Working knowledge of FAA small UAS regulations and operational best practices.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to translate flight behavior into engineering insights.
  • Strong situational awareness and adherence to test-site safety standards.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with fixed-wing RC aircraft operations (huge plus).
  • Familiarity with PX4, ArduPilot, Auterion, and Herelink.
  • Technical background in UAS systems, aerodynamics, or flight controls integration.
  • Ability to record and share video footage of recent acro line-of-sight FPV flights for evaluation.
  • Previous work in structured flight test environments or R&D programs.

Compensation

Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

See below for paid time off details:

  • For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year.
  • For hourly roles: vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week).
The national base pay range for this position within the United States, including Illinois and Colorado.
$28.40—$41.80 USD

About DoorDash

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Above and beyond discrimination and harassment based on “protected categories,” we also strive to prevent other subtler forms of inappropriate behavior (i.e., stereotyping) from ever gaining a foothold in our office. Whether blatant or hidden, barriers to success have no place at DoorDash. We value a diverse workforce – people who identify as women, non-binary or gender non-conforming, LGBTQIA+, American Indian or Native Alaskan, Black or African American, Hispanic or Latinx, Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, differently-abled, caretakers and parents, and veterans are strongly encouraged to apply. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, and any other state or local hiring regulations, we will consider for employment any qualified applicant, including those with arrest and conviction records, in a manner consistent with the applicable regulation.
