About the job

Job summary

The Government Internal Audit Agency (GIAA) is driven by its unparalleled access across government to build ‘better insights, better outcomes’ for our clients.

This role offers a strong platform for career progression within the Agency and the wider civil service, providing opportunities to develop leadership, stakeholder engagement and strategic relationship management skills across government.

The Agency’s unique access across the public sector exposes you to different risk and control environments, allowing you to gain insights, apply experience, contribute meaningfully, and continue developing professionally.


Job description

The role of Corporate Governance and Transparency Manager is part of the Governance team, which sits within the Corporate Services division. This small but dynamic team provides a wide array of corporate governance services, including managing governance frameworks, risk management processes, and internal controls within the GIAA.

The Corporate Governance and Transparency Manager holds a pivotal position within the Governance team and across the Agency. Working closely with senior colleagues, you will ensure the seamless delivery of a high-quality internal governance
function. You will serve as the Agency’s lead on propriety, ethics, correspondence handling, and transparency reporting.

Role responsibilities
Deliver high-quality corporate governance aligned with best practice, ensuring accountability, transparency, and integrity across the Agency by developing, maintaining, and continuously improving governance policies, procedures, and frameworks to ensure they are effective, proportionate, and accessible.
Promote compliance with corporate governance policies and ethical standards, including conflicts of interest, gifts, and hospitality, through assurance checks and by embedding a culture of accountability and transparency.
Oversee transparency and information governance requirements, including publication schemes and external reporting obligations.
Lead the development and continuous improvement of correspondence management policies and procedures in line with regulatory and statutory requirements (e.g., UK GDPR, FOIA, Data (Use and Access) Act 2025) and ensuring alignment with organisational policies, Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) expectations, and lessons learned.
Manage external correspondence processes including Freedom of Information requests, Data Subject Access Requests, complaints, and enquiries.
Manage the Agency's whistleblowing arrangements, ensuring compliance with organisational policies while maintaining confidentiality and protecting the integrity of the process.
Support effective organisational decision making by managing and delivering high-quality committee secretary services, preparing and presenting reports, analysis, and recommendations to senior committees. Provide governance advice and guidance to Directors, Board members, and colleagues as required.
Manage and/or contribute to governance projects and complex work programmes as required. Examples include implementing innovative governance systems and practices, managing Non-Executive Director recruitment, co-ordinating the production of the Annual Report, and co-ordinating governance effectiveness reviews.
Task manage and support the development of the Governance Support Officer (Executive Officer).
Maintain an up-to-date understanding of government, regulatory, legal, political, and technological developments relevant to corporate governance.

Person specification

1.Strong knowledge of relevant legislation, including the Freedom of Information (FOI) Act 2000, Environmental Information Regulations, the General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR), the Data Protection Act 2018, and the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.
2.Proven experience in managing and responding to external correspondence, including complaints, FOI requests, and Data Subject Access Requests, in compliance with statutory timescales and organisational standards, with the ability to maintain strict confidentiality and ensure compliant information management.
3.Experience servicing senior governance committees, helping to shape strategic agendas and working independently to produce high-quality minutes, author and quality assure papers, and track agreed actions.
4.Ability to identify, assess, and mitigate risks through proactive monitoring and effective controls, while taking initiative to lead areas of responsibility with a positive, solution-focused approach demonstrated by a strong track record of delivering or improving administrative processes and efficiencies.
5.Excellent planning and organisational skills with experience managing reactive and proactive workloads and delivering complex work programmes. Adept at prioritising, adapting to change, and staying resilient. Collaborative, with a proven ability to work with stakeholders and teams to achieve shared goals.
6.A confident decision maker, exercising good judgement and with experience of providing high-quality advice to a wide range of colleagues, including senior stakeholders.
7.Task management experience, including supporting and developing team members to achieve high-quality outcomes, managing performance, and embedding accountability.

To apply for this role, you will need to submit your employment history, personal details and provide a statement of suitability of up to 1,000 words, referring to the person specification.

Interviews will be held on Teams.

At the start of the formal interview, candidates will have an opportunity to demonstrate their subject matter expertise and technical skills when they meet with members of the governance team. Details will be provided with the invitation.

The technical skills being assessed are:

  • Comprehension skills
  • Subject matter understanding
  • Practical application
  • Audience awareness
  • Presentation and professional judgement

Candidates will be asked to provide feedback to the interview panel on their experience of meeting with the governance team. This will be followed by a series of questions from the panel. Candidates will receive one score for their presentation and content, and a separate score for their responses to follow-up questions.

At interview, candidates will be assessed on experience and strengths

title: Senior Executive Protection & Protective Security Advisor
description:
The Senior Executive Protection & Protective Security Advisor is responsible for the planning, coordination and delivery of executive protection and protective security services for senior executives and designated personnel across the UK and Northern Europe.

The role combines strategic risk management with operational delivery, ensuring executives can travel, work and engage globally with confidence. Acting as a trusted security partner to executive offices, regional security teams and external providers, the successful candidate will deliver a discreet, intelligence-led and white-glove protective service while maintaining the highest standards of professionalism, confidentiality and client service.

This position is suited to an experienced corporate security professional with a strong executive protection background, capable of operating confidently within C-suite environments, conducting detailed risk assessments, coordinating complex travel and event security arrangements, and deploying operationally as a Personal Protection Officer (PPO) when required.

Requirements

Key Responsibilities

Executive Protection Operations

  • Support the day-to-day delivery of the executive protection programme across the UK and Northern Europe.
  • Coordinate protective security activities for senior executives and designated personnel.
  • Deploy as a Personal Protection Officer (PPO) when required.
  • Maintain oversight of operational tasking, resource allocation and service delivery across all protective activities.
  • Ensure all executive protection operations are delivered professionally, discreetly and in accordance with organisational standards.

Protective Intelligence & Risk Management

  • Conduct comprehensive threat, vulnerability and risk assessments for executives, travel, events and strategic business activities.
  • Analyse security threats and develop practical mitigation strategies tailored to executive profiles and operational requirements.

title: Director Digital Strategy
description:

Digital Strategy & Optimization

Organic Discovery & Content

  • Serve as a strategic partner to marketing, creative, product, engineering, and analytics teams

  • Manage relationships with external agencies, vendors, and technology partners
  • Provide exceptional experiences for our guests, partners, and team members, including by adhering to our appearance and presentation guidelines while on-site.

What do you need to succeed?

  • Extensive digital marketing and web experience with demonstrated effectiveness in driving engagement, conversion, and retention across multi-channel (email, SMS/MMS, paid, and owned) ecosystems.
  • 5+ years leading cross-functional digital teams, including SEO/GEO, UI/UX, analytics, content, and lifecycle/CRM marketing with proven track record owning end-to-end digital ecosystems (website, content, performance, lifecycle channels)
  • Deep expertise with headless/composable CMS platforms (e.g., Hygraph, Optimizely, or equivalent), including content modeling, API-driven delivery, and multi-channel publishing

title: Senior Program Manager, Business Integration
description:
CoinDesk is the most trusted media, events, indices and data company for the global crypto economy. Since 2013, CoinDesk Media has led the story of the future of money and investing, illuminating the transformation in society and culture that comes with it. Our award-winning team of journalists delivers news and unparalleled insights that bring transparency, comprehension and context. CoinDesk Events gathers the global crypto, blockchain and Web3 communities at annual events such as Consensus, the world’s largest and longest-running crypto festival. CoinDesk Indices offers expertise in digital asset indices, data and research to educate and empower investors. For more information on CoinDesk media and events, please visit http://coindesk.com [coindesk.com] and for breaking headlines, data and indices visit http://coindeskmarkets.com [coindeskmarkets.com]

In November 2023, CoinDesk was acquired by the Bullish group, owner of Bullish, a regulated, digital assets exchange. For more information on Bullish, please visit . CoinDesk operates as an independent subsidiary with an editorial committee to protect journalistic independence.

Reports to:

Director - PMO, Change & Delivery

About the Role

Bullish is redefining the capital markets infrastructure by bridging traditional equity systems with blockchain-based tokenization. To drive this vision forward, we are seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead the post-merger integration (PMI) of an established, blue-chip financial services leader into our nimble, hyper-scalable organization. You will own the day-to-day execution of this integration, transforming our post-merger strategy into a cohesive, high-performing model while operating at the strategic altitude required to align C-suite executives and global leaders across both businesses and our broader ecosystem.

This is a highly unique and impactful opportunity. The work you do here will directly impact the future state of our combined business, and position Bullish as an enduring leader in the next chapter of capital markets infrastructure. If this sounds like you, we would love to hear from you.

This position will be required to work onsite at our NYC office a minimum of 4 days per week.

Key Responsibilities:

Business Integration & Operational Modernization:

  • Cross-Functional Execution: Lead and execute the end-to-end integration of core functional lines: People & Organization, Technology, Finance & Accounting, Legal & Compliance, Cost Synergies, and Communications & Branding.

  • Operations Modernization: Identify manual operations and redundant backend processes across both businesses and our broader ecosystem; partner with Executive Leadership to drive automation, efficiency, and cross-platform synergies.

  • Functional Architecture Alignment: Maintain high-level oversight of enterprise system integrations (HRIS, ERP, Cloud, SaaS). Ensure operational workflows are correctly structured around legal entities, cost centers, lines of business, and governance frameworks to safeguard future-state scalability.

Workforce Planning & Resource Optimization:

  • Plan Execution: Translate pre-established capacity analysis into actionable, long-term resource allocation strategies across Technology, Operations, and Compliance.

  • Data-Driven Modeling: Partner with Finance, HR, and Operations to build and refine dynamic human capital, budget, and infrastructure utilization models.

  • Pipeline Readiness: Align staffing models with Executive Leaders to ensure Product, Engineering, Operations, and Regulatory teams are equipped to handle incoming tokenization and digital asset pipelines.

  • Financial Alignment: Continuously monitor integration milestones against cost-synergy targets and revenue milestones.

Stakeholder Alignment & Change Leadership

  • Executive Presence: Manage geographically distributed, highly matrixed technical and non-technical stakeholders—from operational managers to C-Suite executives.

  • Tailored Communication: Navigate varying levels of organizational buy-in by clearly articulating the "why" behind strategic shifts, fostering trust, and driving consensus across distinct corporate cultures.

  • Autonomous Problem Solving: Lead with absolute ownership. Unblock operational bottlenecks independently while exercising sound judgment on when to escalate key risks to executive sponsors.

Risk, Governance & Issue Management

  • Risk Register Ownership: Maintain a living risk register tracking issues, decisions, and escalations, reporting status regularly to the executive sponsor.

  • Interdependency Management: Map cross-workstream dependencies to prevent sequencing failures and resolve blockers early.

  • Escalation Protocols: Enforce clear escalation frameworks, solving problems autonomously and escalating key risks appropriately.

  • Governance Cadence: Run steering committee meetings, workstream syncs, and executive reporting to ensure full visibility into progress, risks, and decisions.

Qualifications & Expertise:

  • Experience: 10+ years in Program Management or Management Consulting, leading complex Post-Merger Integrations (PMI), carve-outs, or enterprise-wide operational transformations.

  • Domain Knowledge: Core understanding of capital markets infrastructure, corporate enterprise workflows, and a strong interest in digital assets, tokenized securities, and stablecoins.

  • Analytical Capability: Proven track record of converting capacity metrics, headcount data, and operational analytics into sustainable resource allocation plans.

  • Soft Skills & Maturity: High emotional intelligence, professional maturity, and the ability to balance empathy with decisive accountability during periods of enterprise change.

  • Education & Certifications: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Engineering, or a related field. PMP, Agile/Scrum, or M&A-specific certifications are preferred.

Preferred Experience:

  • Leading large-scale operational modernizations or business integrations requiring enterprise-wide process adoption.

  • Directing change management programs aligned with core financial systems or regulatory frameworks.

title: National Collection of Pathogenic Viruses (NCPV) Virologist
description:
• Job grade: Higher Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Type of role: Science, Other
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Scientific Campus Porton

About the job

Job summary

This post is positioned within Culture Collections on the Porton site. UKHSA Culture Collections provides authenticated bacteria, viruses, fungi and cell cultures and associated services to the biomedical research and diagnostic communities.

The National Collection of Pathogenic Viruses (NCPV) supplies well characterised, authenticated human pathogenic viruses of importance to human health to the scientific community according to national and international guidelines. The collection comprises viruses that require handling at UK Hazard Group 2 and Hazard Group 3.

The NCPV Virologist role is the focal point for in vitro virology within the team, utilising a wide range of core virology techniques and molecular methods required to authenticate the viral banks produced.

The postholder will be responsible for growing and authenticating viruses for accession into the NCPV catalogue. The postholder will also be responsible for providing technical support for inventory management and the dispatch of restricted products to customers.

Job description

  • To be responsible for day-to-day culture, titration and authentication of Hazard Group 2 and 3 viruses in NCPV.
  • Provide reports through the interpretation and analysis of data, using software and databases as necessary, to make new banks of virus available through NCPV and for associated presentations and publications
  • Assist with the preparation and dispatch of restricted products to customers.
  • To ensure that all work is carried out in accordance with the UKHSA’s Code of Safety Practice and to work within any Quality Systems that are applicable to the site (ISO 9001, ISO 17025).

Detailed job description and main responsibilities

The National Collection of Pathogenic Viruses (NCPV) supplies well characterised, authenticated viruses of importance to human health to the scientific community according to national and international guidelines. The collection comprises viruses that require handling at UK Hazard Group 2 and Hazard Group 3.

The NCPV Virologist role is the focal point for in vitro virology within the team, utilising a wide range of core virology techniques and molecular methods required to authenticate the viral banks produced.

The postholder will be responsible for growing and authenticating Hazard Group 2 and Hazard Group 3 viruses for accession into the NCPV catalogue.

The postholder will also be responsible for providing support for inventory management and the dispatch of restricted products to customers.

This post is positioned within Culture Collections on the Porton Down site.

Main Duties:

  • Plan, implement and utilise a range of methods in support of activities associated with the operation of NCPV to ensure virus banking and quality control targets are met.
  • Assist the NCPV team to identify, evaluate and adapt new technologies where appropriate and to ensure that all activities operate to a high scientific standard using current methods.
  • Provide reports through the interpretation and analysis of data, using software and databases as necessary, to accession NCPV viruses and for presentations and publications
  • To ensure that all work is carried out in accordance with the UKHSA’s Code of Safety Practice and to work within any Quality Systems that are applicable to the site (ISO 9001, ISO 17025).
  • Take responsibility for the running of the NCPV Containment Level 2 laboratory and for the provision of reagents and consumables required for the NCPV project area.
  • Assist with the training and supervision of junior staff allocated to the NCPV as required.
  • Assist with product inventory checking and the preparation and the dispatch of restricted products to Culture Collections customers.

The job holder will undertake the full range of work with people on probation before and after sentence. In accordance with current immigration rules, this role is not eligible for a new Skilled Worker visa.

HM Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS) cannot consider sponsoring you to work as a probation services officer unless you have held a Skilled Worker visa prior to the 22 July 2025 changes.
If you have held a Skilled Worker visa continuously, please raise this during your pre-employment checks and your eligibility will be assessed in accordance with the immigration rules and transitional provisions in place.
If you apply to be a probation services officer and you have not held a Skilled Worker visa prior to 22 July 2025, you will need to consider your options for obtaining and/or maintaining your right to work in the UK in light of these changes.
If your application is successful, you will need to ensure that you have and maintain the legal right to live and work in the Civil Service and in the United Kingdom.

As part of this application, you will also be required to sit the Civil Service Judgement test (CSJT). The CSJT is a two-part test which looks at your ability to make decisions in relation to specific civil service behaviours.

There is also no guarantee that you will progress to the next stages of the recruitment process; however, we will keep you informed at each stage.
Take a look at a short video about Probation Service Officer Role here
About the role
Probation services officers can help make a real difference to peoples’ lives. It’s not always easy to help someone turn their life around, but it can be immensely rewarding.
Probation services officers are required to work within a variety of settings. There may be opportunities for positions within Probation Delivery Units (PDU), Courts, Prisons, Approved Premises etc. depending on business requirement.
Probation services officers are based in a wide variety of settings, listed below:
  • Accredited Programmes
  • Structured Interventions & Attendance Centres
  • Community Accommodation Services
  • Community Integration and Contracts
  • Contracts
  • Courts
  • Integrated Offender Management
  • Performance & Quality
  • Personality Disorder Projects
  • Prisons
  • Public Protection (Custody)
  • Public Protection (Community)
  • The Homeless Prevention Taskforce
  • Service Centre

We’re looking for empathetic, patient and resilient people to join us as probation services officers. As well as making a difference to others, the role offers plenty of on-the-job training and a real chance to build a career in the Probation Service.
As a PSO, you’ll have a similar job to a fully qualified probation officer. The main difference is you’ll work with medium and lower risk people of probation. That’s not to say it’ll be easy. There’s no doubt this is a challenging role.
Day-to-day, you’ll manage a caseload of offenders before and after sentence. We’ll look to you to assess and manage risks, provide information to courts and work closely with agencies throughout the justice system. You’ll also do everything you can to support offenders. This could involve everything from providing practical advice about housing and employment to simply listening and empathising.

You don’t need a degree for this role. We’re much more interested in your personal qualities. Ideally with experience of working with people who have social or personal difficulties, you’ll be empathetic, patient and resilient. Good writing skills are also essential. title: Director, Pharmacy Operations Strategy & Integration
description:
Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Director, Pharmacy Operations Strategy & Integration to join our Pharmacy team.

Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves—one that behaves like a doctor in the family.

About the role:

The Director, Pharmacy Operations Strategy & Integration reports to the SVP, Pharmacy is responsible for shaping and executing Oscar's pharmacy operational excellence agenda for the Pharmacy Clinical Strategy and Operations area. This role translates strategic priorities into a coherent portfolio of operating-model improvements, cross-functional programs, vendor capabilities, and scalable workflows that advance affordability, health outcomes, and the member and provider experience. The Director serves as a connective leader across Pharmacy, Clinical, Product, Engineering, Finance, Actuarial, Concierge, Compliance, and PBM/vendor partners—aligning priorities, decisions, and execution to deliver measurable business impact. This role balances enterprise affordability, member and provider experience, regulatory compliance, operational quality, and long-term scalability as Oscar advances its pharmacy operating model.

You will report into the SVP, Pharmacy.

Work Location: This is a remote position, open to candidates who reside in: Dallas, TX. You will be fully remote; however, our approach to work may adapt over time. Future models could potentially involve a hybrid presence at the hub office associated with your metro area. #LI-Remote

Pay Transparency: The base pay for this role is: $162,453.60 - $213,220.35per year. You are also eligible for employee benefits, participation in Oscar's unlimited vacation program, company equity grants, and annual performance bonuses.

Responsibilities:

  • Set the pharmacy operational excellence strategy, operating rhythm, and execution model, ensuring priorities are aligned to Oscar's enterprise agenda, Pharmacy objectives, affordability goals, and member and provider outcomes.
  • Lead high-priority pharmacy operational transformation initiatives from strategy through execution, including opportunity definition, roadmap development, operational readiness, launch planning, and sustained adoption.
  • Serve as a primary operational partner across internal and external teams, translating pharmacy and PBM opportunities, member and provider needs, and frontline insights into clear priorities, decisions, and measurable outcomes.
  • Stay aware of applicable PBM, pharmacy benefit, managed care, and healthcare regulatory requirements, interpreting the business need and communicating it clearly to internal and external partners so solutions are designed and implemented appropriately.
  • Maintain deep understanding of the pharmacy and healthcare ecosystem, including payer economics, benefit and network dynamics, claims processes, formulary operations, prior authorization workflows, utilization patterns, vendor handoffs, and the drivers of affordability and experience.
  • Partner with cross-functional internal stakeholders and external vendors to manage implementation plans, business reviews, strategic meetings, issue escalation, performance monitoring, and operational integration.
  • Coordinate cross-functionally across Clinical, Pharmacy Operations, Product, Engineering, Finance, Actuarial, Concierge, Compliance, and vendor partners to align decision rights, dependencies, tradeoffs, and delivery plans for high-priority pharmacy initiatives.
  • Serve as an internal consultant and apply an operational excellence lens to diagnose complex process, data, technology, and vendor friction points, then design practical end-to-end solutions that improve throughput, quality, affordability, and member/provider experience.
  • Shape the end-to-end member and provider experience by partnering with Pharmacy, Clinical, Product, Engineering, Concierge, and vendor teams to identify friction points and translate insights into scalable, measurable improvements across pharmacy journeys.
  • Lead governance and executive reporting for pharmacy operational excellence initiatives, synthesizing operational, member, provider, clinical, and financial data into clear priorities, recommendations, and accountability for senior leadership.
  • Identify and manage implementation risks, dependencies, decisions, and change-management needs, ensuring stakeholders understand scope, impact, tradeoffs, and operational readiness requirements.
  • Build repeatable operating playbooks, process standards, controls, and best practices that support a scalable PBM operating model, continuous improvement, and a coherent end-to-end pharmacy experience.
  • Use independent judgment to resolve complex problems, evaluate variable factors, and determine the best course of action for technology-enabled process improvement and operational transformation.
  • Support capacity planning, budget management, business-case development, and value realization measurement for PBM, vendor, and operational excellence initiatives.
  • Ensure operational workflows, vendor capabilities, and program execution meet applicable regulatory, compliance, quality, and contractual requirements.
  • Compliance with all applicable laws and regulations
  • Other duties as assigned

Requirements:

  • 10+ years of experience in healthcare, business operations, strategy and operations, product operations, or program leadership.
  • 7+ years of Managed Care, PBM, pharmacy operations, clinical operations, or related healthcare payer experience.
  • 5+ years leading large-scale, cross-functional strategy, operational transformation, or implementation initiatives from opportunity definition through launch and adoption.
  • 5+ years partnering directly with cross-functional business, Product, Engineering, vendor, or operations teams to set priorities, define requirements, influence solutions, and deliver business outcomes.
  • Experience interpreting regulatory, compliance, operational, or contractual business needs and translating them into actionable requirements for cross-functional partners.
  • Experience with strategic planning, roadmapping, business analysis, operational readiness, change management, and translating priorities into executable cross-functional plans.
  • Experience translating complex operational data and performance information into executive-level insights, recommendations, and governance materials.
  • Experience managing budgets, capacity models, business cases, or financial performance for operational or transformation initiatives.

Bonus points:

  • MBA, MPH, Master's degree in Business Administration or a related field preferred.
  • Management consulting, internal strategy and operations, process engineering, Lean, Six Sigma, or similar structured problem-solving experience.
  • Experience with PBM implementation, pharmacy benefit administration, claims adjudication, formulary operations, prior authorization, rebate/formulary systems, or healthcare data feeds.
  • Experience working in a matrixed teams through enterprise transformation, implementation, or operational excellence work.

title: Associate Software Engineer (Seasonal)
description:
Major League Baseball is looking for an Associate Software Engineer (Seasonal) in the Baseball and Content Engineering (BACE) organization to build the code that powers the baseball experience on MLB.com. Launched in 2001 as the tech arm of Major League Baseball, MLB.com is renowned for creating experiences that baseball fans love, and by embracing modern, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-augmented development practices, we're building the future of sports technology faster than ever. Our BACE organization distributes content from our Content Management System (CMS) to MLB, MiLB, and other operated properties. This includes managing the publishing pipelines for news, videos, and push notifications, as well as services that support sitemap generation, search functionality, and cache busting. Additionally, we support internal tools that enable digital producers to create and manage forms for both MLB and MiLB Clubs. We also maintain a tool for managing player photo uploads, marketing materials, walk-up songs, and vanity redirects. This role offers the opportunity to collaborate with other world-class engineers, product developers, and designers; contribute to award-winning, complex apps and systems; influence the innovation of products used by millions globally; and work in a highly collaborative, results-oriented team environment.

Responsibilities

Coding & Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Augmented Development

  • Work in a Full-stack capacity across JavaScript (Node, React, Next.js) and Java (Spring Boot)
  • Leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI) coding assistants and agentic tools to scaffold code, optimize logic, and accelerate the delivery of robust features
  • Write clean, concise, modular code that is easily testable, taking full ownership and accountability for reviewing and refining any Artificial Intelligence (AI)-generated code
  • Utilize Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to assist in writing comprehensive unit and integration tests, ensuring high code quality and coverage

Collaboration & Modern Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)

  • Participate in a modern, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enhanced agile environment
  • Participate in the full software development lifecycle (requirements gathering, designing, building, testing, and maintenance), utilizing agentic tools to streamline documentation and technical planning
  • Participate in code reviews with other team members, critically evaluating human-written and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted code for security, performance, and architectural alignment

Qualifications & Skills

  • Bachelor's Degree or equivalent experience in a related field (Computer Science, Computer Engineering)
  • 0-2 years of experience in Java and the Spring Boot framework
  • Experience with front-end web development
  • Understanding of unit, integration, and end-to-end testing
  • Understanding of modern agile processes, including continuous delivery, automated testing, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted workflows
  • Familiarity with Artificial Intelligence (AI) coding assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Codeium) and an aptitude for prompt-driven development

Preferred Experience

  • Experience with front-end technologies including React
  • Experience with back-end technologies including Spring and Node
  • Experience with HyperText Markup Language (HTML) or Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) layouts
  • Experience using Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to aid in debugging, code scaffolding, or generating test coverage
  • Experience with GraphQL and data federation
  • Experience working with cloud-native tooling such as Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform
  • Experience contributing to open source projects
  • Experience with public cloud providers such as Google Cloud
  • Experience with content delivery networks such as Cloudflare, Fastly
  • Familiarity with building or integrating Large Language Models (LLMs), Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents, or Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines
  • A baseball fan or sports enthusiast

Pay Range: $40.00 - $55.00 per hour

The actual offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your work experience, education, skills, and any other factors MLB considers relevant to the hiring decision.

Why MLB?

Major League Baseball (MLB) is the most historic of the major professional sports leagues in the United States and Canada. Employees love working at MLB because of the culture of growth, teamwork, and professionalism. Employees who are most successful at MLB take initiative, know how to identify problems and provide solutions, and always put the Team first. For those ready to step up to the plate and join the major leagues, MLB takes the same approach as teams do with their players: empowering our “workforce athletes” to be at their best by engineering experiences that put employees in the best position to succeed. Major League Baseball is looking for candidates who are passionate about growing America’s pastime to best serve its fans for decades to come.

California Residents: Please see our California Recruitment Privacy Policy for more details.

Colorado Residents: Colorado based applicants may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application and hiring process, please email us at accommodations@mlb.com. Requests received for non-disability related issues, such as following up on an application, will not receive a response.

title: Director of Communications
location: Birmingham, Leeds and London. With expectation of regular travel and to be present for in-person meetings with ministers where required. We currently work on a hybrid basis with 60% of our time working
description:
• Job grade: SCS Pay Band 2
  • Contract type: Permanent
  • Business area: DFT - Decarbonisation, Technology & Strategy Group (DTS)
  • Type of role: Senior leadership
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Birmingham, Leeds and London. With expectation of regular travel and to be present for in-person meetings with ministers where required. We currently work on a hybrid basis with 60% of our time working in an office location working

About the job

Job summary

The Director of Communications leads the Department’s communications team and is Head of Profession for communications staff across the group. You will join Directors of Communications across government leading a fundamental transformation in how the government informs and connects with citizens in an era of rapid technological change, evolving media consumption, and the critical challenge of building public trust.

You will be the Secretary of State’s senior official communications adviser. You will set communications strategy, ensure high performance delivery, and promote a culture of innovation and improve professional standards across the DfT Group. You will be responsible for a wide range of communications activity that supports the Department’s Strategic Outcomes and the Government’s agenda.

Audience-focused and insight-driven, you will bring consumer marketing and storytelling expertise to public service communication. You will boldly champion modern communications - leading the cultural shift from reactive, press-first communications to integrated always-on campaigns, embracing digital innovation, leveraging responsible AI and boldly putting citizens at the heart of our planning and delivery.

You will influence and inform stakeholders inside and outside of Government. You will be able to lead highly effective public and media relations activity, high impact campaign delivery, and targeted stakeholder engagement.

Across the Group you will be accountable for communications strategy, spend and professional standards across the Department’s network of agencies and other bodies, providing professional leadership to all communications staff across this network, and providing the transformational leadership required to keep pace with the rapidly changing media and communications landscape.

You will role model continuous professional development and make sure the Department for Transport’s communications function has the capability and skills it needs to deliver the communications strategy.

You will be part of a senior peer network of Government Communications leaders, collectively responsible for a Civil Service profession of 7,000 communicators across departments, agencies and arm’s-length bodies. As a leader within GCS you will play an active role in raising professional standards and improving efficiency more broadly, including by leading continuous improvement projects.

Job description

  • Government Directors of Communications come from a diverse range of backgrounds and experience, including digital and advertising agencies, journalism, television production, marketing, PR, as well as Corporate Public Affairs and not for profit and private sectors. We are less prescriptive about background and are more interested in the skills and behaviours you can bring, with focus on expertise and leadership.
  • What matters most is your ability to think strategically, lead transformation, champion innovation whilst navigating complexity, and deliver measurable impact through audience-first communications.
  • Accomplished storyteller – articulate, intelligent, pragmatic and creative. Creating stories and narratives that speak to audiences. Knowing when and how to communicate to influence stakeholders, drive behaviour change and deliver impact.
  • Influencer and shaper – Politically savvy, emotionally intelligent and tuned in to the needs of different stakeholder groups. Experience advising and influencing at the most senior levels (Board, Ministerial or equivalent).
  • Strategic thinker – grasps the organisational mission and central priorities, building insight-informed strategies and plans. Results and impact focused, while alive to reputational risks and the need to be adaptable to changes around you.
  • Audience advocate – in a rapidly evolving media landscape, recognises the importance of audience and how to harness the most effective digital platforms, traditional media, relationships and networks to build engagement and/or behaviour change.
  • Team leader – collaborative, inclusive style. An inspiring leader who builds and develops multidisciplinary teams, fostering an environment of creativity, growth and high performance
  • System leader – Commitment to collective impact across Government, not just departmental outcomes. Brings collaboration, compromise, pace and courage to cross-government working. Models behaviours that signal to teams that system-wide transformation is the future of the profession.

Person specification

You will need to be able to show, through your application, that you have the professional skills, breadth of experience and personal qualities for this post, as well as the leadership skills to succeed at Director level in the Senior Civil Service.

You will be an exceptional senior communications leader with a strong track record of delivery for large, complex organisations. You will be able to demonstrate your capability and potential against the following essential criteria:

  • Marketing and storytelling mindset with demonstrable experience of audience-led, insight-driven campaigns. You understand segmentation, targeting and positioning. You have proven success developing multi-channel campaigns and creative content strategies with clear evaluation metrics and measurable impact—including large-scale behaviour-change or trust-building campaigns.
  • Senior advisory and influencing skills – excellent interpersonal and influencing skills as a trusted adviser to diverse stakeholders internally and externally, including at Board, C-suite or ministerial (or equivalent) level. You have a track record of influencing senior decision-making, demonstrating political acuity, strategic judgement and emotional intelligence in highly visible and sensitive environments.
  • Proven crisis management and transformation leadership - experience leading communications transformation with excellent judgement to manage crises, reputational risk and politically sensitive issues. An awareness of public sentiment and proven experience using this information to inform decision-making.
  • Exceptional leadership of multi-disciplinary teams – a resilient and transformational leader with experience of building capability and fostering a creative, inclusive and impact-focussed team. You create a clear vision, inspire performance and lead teams through complexity and change.

Benefits

Alongside your salary of £120,000, Department for Transport contributes £34,764 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

Whatever your role, we take your career and development seriously, and want to enable you to build a really successful career with the Department and wider Civil Service.

It is crucial that our employees have the right skills to develop their careers and meet the challenges ahead, and you’ll benefit from regular performance and development reviews to ensure this development is ongoing. As a Civil Service employee, you’ll be entitled to a large range of benefits.

Equality, Diversity & Inclusion

The Civil Service values and supports all its employees.

We have strong and pro-active staff networks, special leave policies for hospital appointments, reasonable adjustments put in place for those who need them, and diversity talent programmes to help everyone irrespective of background, to achieve their potential.

Pension

Your pension is a valuable part of your total reward package.

A competitive contributory pension scheme that you can enter as soon as you join where we will make a significant contribution to the cost of your pension; where your contributions come out of your salary before any tax is taken; and where your pension will continue to provide valuable benefits for you and your family if you are too ill to continue to work or die before you retire. Visit Civil Service Pension Scheme for more details. >

Generous Annual Leave and Bank Holiday Allowance

25 days annual leave on entry, increasing on a sliding scale to 30 days after 5 years’ service (allowance is pro rata for part-time employees). This is in addition to 8 public holidays.

This will be complimented by one further day paid privilege entitlement to mark the King’s Birthday.

Staff Wellbeing

Flexible working including part-time or term-time working and access to Flexible Working Schemes allowing you to vary your working day as long as you work your total hours.

Generous paid maternity and paternity leave which is notably more than the statutory minimum offered by many other employers.

Childcare benefits (policy for new employees as of 5 April 2018): The government has introduced the Tax-Free Childcare (TFC) scheme. Working parents can open an online childcare account and for every £8 they pay in, the government adds £2, up to a maximum of £2000 a year for each child or £4000 for a disabled child. Parents then use the funds to pay for registered childcare. Existing employees may be able to continue to claim childcare vouchers, so please check how the policy would work for you here. Any move to the DfT from another employer will mean you can no longer access childcare vouchers. This includes moves between government departments.

Onsite facilities Opportunity to use onsite facilities including fitness centres and staff canteens (where applicable).

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence

Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

Application

To apply for this post, you will need to complete the online form via Gatenby Sanderson. This should be completed no later than 23:55 on Monday 23rd November 2026.

The application will include:

  • A CV setting out your career history, with key responsibilities and achievements. Please ensure you have provided reasons for any gaps within the last two years. Your CV should be no longer than two A4 pages at font size 12.
  • A Statement of Suitability (no longer than 1000 words) explaining how you consider your personal skills, qualities and experience provide evidence of your suitability for the role, with particular reference to the criteria in the person specification.

Failure to submit both documents will mean the panel only have limited information on which to assess your application against the criteria in the person specification.

As part of the online application process, you will be asked a number of diversity-related questions. If you do not wish to provide a declaration on any of the particular characteristics, you will have the option to select 'prefer not to say’.

All monitoring data will be treated in the strictest confidence and will not be provided to the selection panel.

Should you encounter any issues with your application please get in touch with us via devon.coates-leaning@gatenbysanderson.com

Your application will be acknowledged when it is received.

For a confidential discussion to help inform your application, please contact our recruitment advisors at Gatenby Sanderson:

Orla.Brennan@gatenbysanderson.com

Olivia.Robinson@gatenbysanderson.com

Selection Process and Shortlist​

Stephen Cohen, Civil Service Commissioner, will chair the process. More detailed information can be found at the Civil Service Commission website: Civil Service Commission ​

Stephen will be joined by:​

  • Ross Gribbin, Director General, Decarbonisation, Technology and Strategy Group, DfT;
  • A senior representative from the Government Communication Service;
  • A member of the HR leadership team, DfT​.

The panel will select a shortlist of candidates whose applications best demonstrate suitability for the role, by considering the evidence provided against the essential criteria set out in the Person Specification.​

Candidates applying under the Disability Confident Scheme who meet the minimum selection criteria in the job specification are guaranteed an interview.​

Assessment

Shortlisted candidates may be asked to take part in a series of assessments which could include:

  • Staff Engagement Exercise - a presentation and Q&A with a representative staff group from across the DfT.

These assessments will not result in a pass or fail decision. Rather, they are designed to support the panel’s decision making and highlight areas for the panel to explore further at interview.

Informal Discussion

Shortlisted candidates will have the opportunity to speak to Ross Gribbin prior to the final interview. This is an informal discussion to allow candidates to learn more about the role and is not part of the assessment process.

Ministerial Meeting

Prior to appointment, shortlisted candidates will be required to meet with Heidi Aleander, Secretary of State for Transport, further information will be provided.

Interview

You will be asked to attend a panel interview in order to have a more in-depth discussion of your previous experience and professional competence in relation to the criteria set out in the Person Specification.

Interviews are expected to take place face to face in our London office, all shortlisted candidates will be asked to prepare a 5 minute presentation.


Offer and Feedback

Unfortunately, due to the anticipated number of applicants for this role, we are unable to provide feedback to those not successful at shortlist stage. Candidates who are shortlisted and attend an interview will be offered verbal feedback from a member of the interview panel.

The timeline later in this pack indicates the date by which decisions are expected to be made, all candidates will be advised of the outcome as soon as possible thereafter, and we will advise on any delays.

Expected Timeline

We will try and offer as much flexibility as we can, but it may not be possible to offer alternative dates for assessments or interviews. You are therefore asked to note the below timetable, exercising flexibility through the recruitment and selection process, in order to meet the dates given. Please note that these dates may be subject to change.

The anticipated timetable is as follows:

Advert Closing Date: 23:55 Monday 23rd November 2026

Longlist: c30th November 2026

Shortlist: w/c 14th December 2026

Assessments/Ministerial Discussion : w/c 4th and 11th January 2027

Panel Interviews: w/c 18th January 2027

Reasonable Adjustments

We are committed to making reasonable adjustments in order to support disabled job applicants and ensure that you are not disadvantaged in the recruitment and assessment process.

If you feel that you may need a reasonable adjustment to be made, or you would like to discuss your requirements in more detail, please contact:

olivia.robinson@gatenbysanderson.com in the first instance.

Further Information

If your application is successful but you have been dismissed from the Civil Service, your application could be removed at the pre-employment checking stage depending on the nature of the dismissal.

Applicants who are successful at interview will be, as part of pre-employment screening, subject to a check on the Internal Fraud Database (IFD). This check will provide information about employees who have been dismissed for fraud or dishonesty offences. This check also applies to employees who resign or otherwise leave before being dismissed for fraud or dishonesty had their employment continued. Any applicant’s details held on the IFD will be refused employment. A candidate is not eligible to apply for a role within the Civil Service if the application is made within a 5-year period following a dismissal for carrying out internal fraud against government.

All external applicants and current employees of accredited non-departmental public bodies (NDPBs) will be required to undergo a Social Media Check. A Social Media Check is a review of your publicly available online activity, typically across platforms like LinkedIn, Facebook, X (formerly Twitter), Instagram, and others. The purpose is to identify any public posts or content that could raise concerns for employers, such as:

  • Hate speech or discriminatory behaviour
  • Threats or acts of violence
  • Illegal activity or substance misuse
  • Sexually explicit material
  • Extremist views or affiliations

Importantly, this check does not involve hacking into your accounts or accessing private messages. It only considers content you have chosen to make public. Employers use this kind of screening to help ensure their workplace remains safe, inclusive, and aligned with company values. It’s not about judging your personality or lifestyle - it’s about checking for potential red flags that might affect the role or company culture. If you have questions or concerns about the social media check, we would be happy to explain in more detail what’s being looked at and how your data is handled securely and fairly.



Feedback will only be provided if you attend an interview or assessment.
This role has a minimum assignment duration of 3 years. An assignment duration is the period of time a Senior Civil Servant is expected to remain in the same post to enable them to deliver on the agreed key business outcomes. The assignment duration also supports your career through building your depth of expertise.

As part of accepting this role you will be agreeing to the expected assignment duration set out above. This will not result in a contractual change to your terms and conditions. Please note this is an expectation only, it is not something which is written into your terms and conditions or indeed which the employing organisation or you are bound by. It will depend on your personal circumstances at a particular time and business needs, for example, would not preclude any absence like family friendly leave. It is nonetheless an important expectation, which is why we ask you to confirm you agree to the assignment duration set out above.

Security

Successful candidates must meet the security requirements before they can be appointed. The level of security needed is security check (opens in a new window).

See our vetting charter (opens in a new window).

title: Leasing Consultant
description:
At Bozzuto, every team member shares a deep commitment to doing good for those around us. We live this each day by designing, building, managing and maintaining one-of-a-kind residences. Whether it’s the talent within our communities or the expertise across our property operations teams, we work together to make extraordinary happen for our clients, residents and fellow team members.

Our people are dedicated to delivering exceptional experiences to everyone we serve including each other. This shared purpose drives us to excel in every role and fosters a welcoming, inclusive workplace where teamwork thrives. Guided by our core values of concern, creativity, passion and the pursuit of perfection, we are inspired and empowered to reach higher, unlock our full potential and be truly extraordinary.

Primary Responsibilities:

You’re caring and take pride in making peoples’ day better. You value connections and engaging in meaningful conversations. Your genuine desire to make people feel at home makes you a natural at solving problems for our customers.

As a Sales & Marketing Associate (Leasing Consultant), your primary responsibilities include:

  • Converting leads into community tours by following up with all prospects and providing helpful and compelling information about the community and neighborhood
  • Conducting informative and personalized tours of the apartment community that result in new leases
  • Building brand loyalty by ensuring that the resident experience is consistently stellar
  • Generating awareness, interest and excitement via social media
  • Working weekends when prospective residents are out looking for their new home—three weekends per month with two days off during the week

What You Bring to Us:

  • A customer-focused mentality
  • Outstanding communication skills both written and verbal
  • Proficient in leveraging social media platforms such as Facebook and Instagram, and a passion to create and deliver engaging and distinctive content.
  • A sharp professional appearance
  • Sales aptitude
  • Competent with various software, apps and computer programs

This position is eligible for additional bonus opportunities.

Salary Range
$49,000—$50,000 USD
When you join Bozzuto, you're not just accepting a job; you are becoming part of a community that cares about your overall well-being and professional growth. We recognize that our team members are the core of our business, and we are committed to taking care of them so they can deliver outstanding experiences to our residents. In addition to an award-winning culture, our benefits take into consideration everything from career development, retirement, family matters and health and wellness.
Working on our team and in this position, you can expect:
  • Competitive compensation.
  • Health & wellness benefits. We offer coverage for medical, dental, and vision, including access to the best doctors at an affordable price.
  • Paid leave. We provide 20 days of paid time off plus holidays.
  • Retirement planning. We offer a 401k program with a company match.
  • Tuition reimbursement. Plus, many other programs to support career development and growth.
  • A place you belong. We proudly offer a diverse range of employee resource groups, providing opportunities for our employees to connect over shared experiences, backgrounds, and cultures.

Bozzuto is proudly an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Bozzuto uses AI-enabled tools to enhance candidate sourcing in the recruitment process by helping identify qualified candidates for open positions.

title: Data Surveillance Information Officer
description:
• Job grade: Executive Officer
  • Contract type: Permanent, Loan, Secondment
  • Length of employment: Permanent
  • Type of role: Other
  • Working pattern: Flexible working, Full-time, Job share, Part-time
  • Number of jobs available: 1

Location

Fareham, Ashford, Chilton or Horsham

About the job

Job summary

UKHSA’s local Health Protection Teams (HPTs) play a central role in protecting public health by working with partners to deliver surveillance, monitoring, operational support, advice, education, training and research.

The Data Surveillance Information Officer (DSIO) is essential to delivering HPT objectives, providing expert information management and administrative support to ensure efficient service delivery. Working closely with colleagues across the Health Protection Team and Field Services, the postholder helps maintain a coordinated and responsive health protection service.

The role supports clinical incident management from a data perspective, strengthens governance processes and promotes high standards of data quality. By collaborating with Acute Response Duty Teams, the DSIO provides data analysis, information and operational insight to support informed decision-making and timely responses to emerging challenges.

You are responsible for supporting the flow, storage and retrieval of data across the regional team, ensuring data integrity, analysis and reporting. They also contribute to the development of information systems and liaise with external organisations where required.

The DSIO works with Consultants in Health Protection, microbiologists and other professional staff, ensuring routine and ad hoc reports are produced and shared, while supporting regional health protection activities, including outbreak and incident investigations.

Working for your organisation

We pride ourselves as being an employer of choice, where Everyone Matters promoting equality of opportunity to actively encourage applications from everyone, including groups currently underrepresented in our workforce.

UKHSA ethos is to be an inclusive organisation for all our staff and stakeholders. To create, nurture and sustain an inclusive culture, where differences drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our workforce and wider communities. We do this through celebrating and protecting differences by removing barriers and promoting equity and equality of opportunity for all.

Please visit our careers site for more information

Job description

  1. Support clinical staff in managing infectious disease cases and outbreaks through follow-up, coordination of results and data analysis, providing accurate and timely information to the team.
  2. Ensure robust data flow and reporting mechanisms for laboratory and clinical notifications to protect individuals and local populations and support continuous improvement of health protection functions.
  3. Ensure all records are processed and maintained in line with agreed protocols and SOPs; and checks are made on data electronically submitted
  4. Assist the DSS in ensuring timely reporting to the Health Protection team and partner organisations in line with the surveillance reporting calendar.
  5. Develop, manage and maintain surveillance systems and databases for communicable diseases and environmental hazards, ensuring data from all sources is valid and accurately recorded.
  6. Liaise with key surveillance partners including Field Services, Local Authorities, Microbiologists, TB nurses, and regional and national teams.
  7. Ensure surveillance databases remain accurate and consistent, resolving data quality issues.
  8. Audit data and information systems to ensure integrity and reliability and contribute to surveillance quality improvements.
  9. Review and evaluate routine and ad hoc surveillance reports to ensure timely and accurate delivery.
  10. Support outbreak investigations and epidemiological research through reports, graphs and outbreak curves. May participate in food poisoning investigations including questionnaire design, data entry and analysis. May require out-of-hours working with time off in lieu.
  11. Provide CIMS training for staff as required, and Act as CIMS Information Champion for the region.
  12. Attend meetings and working groups representing the Surveillance function and complete associated actions.
  13. Prepare SOPs based on national guidance with health protection clinical staff.
  14. Maintain confidentiality and information security in line with UKHSA policies, the Data Protection Act and Caldicott requirements.
  15. Attend professional meetings, conferences and training as designated by the Manager/Surveillance Lead/Regional Deputy Director.

Professional Development

  1. Identify and address professional development needs through appraisal and development planning, attending relevant training.
  2. Complete all mandatory training, including fire safety and information governance.

Key Working Relationships

The post holder will communicate regularly with a wide range of clinical and non-clinical colleagues within and outside UKHSA.

Internal

  • UKHSA Regional teams
  • Other UKHSA divisions/directorates

External

  • NHS Trust microbiology departments
  • Infection Prevention & Control teams
  • Hospital clinicians, microbiologists and infection control staff
  • Local Authorities
  • General Practitioners and staff
  • Integrated Care Boards

Main Duties

  • Support the data of infectious disease surveillance, notifications, and outbreak data.
  • Maintain accurate databases, reporting systems, and statutory returns (CIMS)
  • Analyse data, produce reports, and support outbreak investigations
  • Ensure data quality, compliance, and information governance standards
  • Collaborate with health partners and provide system training and guidance
  • Develop procedures, represent the surveillance function, and support service improvement

Please note this list is not exhaustive.

Person specification

Essential role criteria:

  • Educated to degree level in numerate discipline, computer science or IT equivalent which demonstrates core statistical skills or have worked in a statistical/data science field and are able to demonstrate continuous professional development in statistics/data science and has an understanding of basic epidemiological terms and methods.
  • Highly proficient in the use of computers, databases, and Microsoft Access, Word and Excel, with experience in data management, analysis, reporting and presentation.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate proactively, accurately and succinctly, and to negotiate effectively with a wide range of health, IT and academic professionals.
  • Strong organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise and coordinate workloads, work independently and collaboratively, and meet tight deadlines.
  • Demonstrates sound numeracy, attention to detail and problem-solving skills, producing accurate, consistent work and dealing with issues calmly, efficiently and in a timely manner.
  • Committed to maintaining confidentiality, undertaking training and participating in continuous professional development.

title: Postdoctoral Associate
description:
Required Qualification\: (as evidenced by an attached resume)
PhD or foreign equivalent in Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Medicinal Chemistry, Chemical Biology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a closely related discipline in hand by the start of the appointment. Experience in synthetic organic chemistry, small-molecule synthesis, reaction development and optimization, and analytical characterization of chemical compounds using techniques such as NMR, LC-MS, and HPLC.

Preferred Qualification\:
Experience in medicinal chemistry, chemical biology, biorthogonal chemistry, design and synthesis of small molecules, structure–activity or structure–reactivity relationship studies, and development of chemical probes. Experience in compound purification, analytical method development, and characterization of chemical stability and purity. Familiarity with mammalian cell culture, fluorescence-based assays, or biological evaluation of small molecules is desirable. Demonstrated record of peer-reviewed publications, strong written and oral communication skills, and ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary research environment.

Job Description\:
A Postdoctoral Associate position is available in the laboratory of Dr. Navjot Pabla in the Division of Nephrology, Department of Medicine, at Stony Brook University. The laboratory investigates molecular mechanisms of acute and chronic kidney diseases with an emphasis on mitochondrial biology, metabolism, kidney injury, and development of novel therapeutics.

The laboratory investigates molecular mechanisms of acute and chronic kidney diseases, with an emphasis on identifying therapeutic targets and developing novel pharmacological approaches for kidney diseases.

The successful candidate will conduct independent and collaborative research focused on the design, synthesis, optimization, and characterization of small molecules and chemical probes for therapeutic discovery. Research will involve synthetic organic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, chemical biology, and analytical approaches to develop and evaluate compounds targeting molecular pathways involved in kidney injury and repair.

Responsibilities include designing and executing synthetic strategies, optimizing chemical reactions, purifying and characterizing compounds using NMR, LC-MS, and HPLC, investigating structure–activity relationships, and collaborating with laboratory members to evaluate compounds in biological systems. The candidate will also analyze and interpret research data, maintain accurate laboratory records, prepare manuscripts for publication, present research findings at scientific meetings, and assist with grant preparation. The position provides opportunities for multidisciplinary collaboration and independent research and career development.

Specific Duties\:

● Design, synthesize, purify, and characterize small molecules and chemical probes for medicinal chemistry and therapeutic discovery projects. Develop and optimize synthetic routes, investigate structure–activity and structure–reactivity relationships, and use analytical techniques including NMR, LC-MS, and HPLC to assess compound identity, purity, and stability. Collaborate with laboratory members to support biological evaluation of compounds in cellular and preclinical models of kidney disease. Analyze research data, prepare manuscripts, and present scientific findings.

● Develop and optimize synthetic and analytical methodologies, maintain accurate laboratory records and research documentation, collaborate with investigators in chemistry, pharmacology, and kidney biology, mentor junior trainees, and contribute to preparation of manuscripts, fellowship applications, and research grants.

● Perform other duties as assigned, including participation in laboratory meetings, departmental seminars, collaborative research activities, and professional development.

Special Notes\:
The Research Foundation of SUNY is a private educational corporation. Employment is subject to the Research Foundation policies and procedures, sponsor guidelines and the availability of funding. FLSA Exempt position, not eligible for the overtime provisions of the FLSA. Minimum salary threshold must be met to maintain FLSA exemption.

title: Referral Specialist
description:
Zinda Law Group is an elite plaintiff’s personal injury and medical malpractice firm looking for ambitious, dynamic, driven, and passionate professionals to join our growing team. We are looking for a Referral Specialist that coordinates incoming attorney referrals and refers cases out. The specialist manages communication, documentation, follow-up, and financial tracking in collaboration with Marketing, Intake, Attorney Teams, Finance, and Referral Partners. We have offices in Texas, Colorado, Arizona, New Mexico, and Florida and serve clients throughout the nation.

We are not your typical law firm, and by joining us, you will have the following opportunities, and many, many more, at your disposal:

  • Valuable, Rewarding Work: Every day, you will be helping people. Our clients come to us after they have been through one of the worst days of their lives, and the work you do here will help them get the justice they deserve and get their lives back on track. Our paralegals play a critical role in our cases and often make lifelong connections with the people we help.
  • Continuous Learning: You will be mentored by and train with top professionals in your field from day one. Our in-house certifications and trainings will help you succeed no matter your level of experience.
  • Remarkable Colleagues: When you join our team, you join a group of diverse individuals who are dedicated and passionate about the work they do every single day.

Responsibilities:

Incoming attorney referrals

  • Receive, acknowledge, and track incoming referrals. Verify the referring firm, attorney contact information, referral source, current representation, and authorization for client contact before outreach.
  • Gather complete intake information, case summaries, available records, and reported deadlines. Coordinate conflict checks and attorney review; flag missing information and urgent issues.
  • Follow each referral through review and an acceptance, decline, or referral decision. Keep the referring firm informed as update requests and coordinate timely client intake and handoff to the assigned legal team.
  • Obtain and save attorney-approved referral agreements, client engagement documents, and supporting records. Record approved fee arrangements and responsibilities, and escalate incomplete or inconsistent referral terms.

Outgoing referrals

  • Maintain the pending referral queue, prepare case summaries, and send complete, authorized referrals to approved firms, following attorney direction and/or firm procedures.
  • Follow up on pending placements; coordinate receiving counsel's written acceptance, attorney-approved referral terms, and required client consent.
  • Draft withdrawal and transfer letters and obtain signed client agreement and consent before completing the transfer.
  • Securely transmit authorized case files, confirm receipt and the receiving attorney's acceptance of representation, and update assignments and status. Route unplaced or declined matters to the responsible attorney and complete approved rejection and file-closing steps.

Ongoing case monitoring

  • Monitor active referred-out cases and cases in which the firm retains an interest through resolution. Obtain status updates at least quarterly, with more frequent follow-up for pending actions, significant developments, or deadlines.
  • Obtain and save applicable documents, including signed agreements, filed petitions or complaints, settlement information, and withdrawal or closure letters. Record changes promptly and escalate missing updates or inconsistent information.

Referral relationships

  • Maintain referral-partner information by state, practice area, case criteria, and availability. Build professional relationships through responsive communication, scheduled check-ins, and feedback on referral quality and service.

Records and financial reporting

  • Keep practice management records and referral trackers current, including referral source, case type, state, responsible firms, status, class codes, agreements, last contact, next follow-up, and attorney-identified deadlines.
  • Save correspondence and documents in designated case folders, protect confidential information, and maintain accurate notes. Audit records regularly, correct discrepancies, and submit Closing File Checklists for review before processing approved closures.
  • Coordinate with Finance to obtain case-cost and trust-liability ledgers when needed, communicate approved expense-reimbursement requests, and track attorney-approved referral fees payable or receivable. Draft Closing Statements, compile payment documentation and confirm receipt and reconciliation with Finance.
  • Prepare scheduled reports on incoming and outgoing referrals, review and placement times, pending and overdue matters, case updates, referral fees, and reimbursable costs. Identify bottlenecks and recommend improvements to the manager.

Required qualifications

  • Bilingual (English and Spanish) communication skills;
  • Paralegal degree, training or certification (ABA approved program);
  • Two years of personal injury or medical malpractice law firm experience in referrals, intake, legal assistant, paralegal, or case coordination;
  • Clear, professional communication with attorneys, referral partners, prospective clients, and clients experiencing stressful circumstances
  • Strong organization, accuracy, and follow-through; ability to manage a high volume of matters, prioritize deadlines, and work independently while following procedures and escalating concerns.
  • Proficiency with practice management or CRM systems, email, spreadsheets, electronic documents, and digital file management; ability to learn the firm's systems and complete required training.
  • Sound judgment with confidential information and a clear understanding of when attorney review or approval is required.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with personal injury or medical malpractice matters, law firm referral relationships, client transfers, or referral-fee tracking.
  • Experience coordinating matters across multiple states;
  • Paralegal training or certification;

Compensation, Benefits & Perks:

  • Compensation Range: Based on Experience, starting at $22/hour
  • Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Retirement Plan with Generous Company Contribution Match
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • Excellent Working Environment
  • Opportunities to work remotely
  • Opportunities for Ongoing Training and Mentoring by Our Outstanding Team
  • Opportunities to Advance and Grow in the Company

We will be accepting applications on an ongoing basis until a candidate is selected for the position.

To apply, please submit a resume and cover letter.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, or other protected status as required by applicable law.

Job summary

The Countermeasures Development and Evaluation Centre is based at Porton and has approximately 250 staff, performing a range of research activities, including high containment level work. The department’s work covers a broad range of projects involving vaccine and therapeutic, discovery, evaluation, development, and research.

The Antimicrobial Development, Discovery and Diagnostics (AD3) team sits in the Countermeasures Development, Evaluation and Preparedness Division in the Public Health Microbiology Directorate within the Chief Scientific Officer Group. Its work focuses on the discovery, development and evaluation of antimicrobial therapies directed at UKHSA priority pathogens, with a particular focus on AMR/emerging pathogens.

The post holder will provide specialist laboratory skills in support of the antivirals ‘Growth through Science’ programme, which is developing an antiviral testing service for use against a wide range of pathogens, the over aim being to identify broad-spectrum antivirals for pandemic preparedness.

Experience of working with cell culture and ACDP2 pathogens are essential, while experience in working with viruses is desirable. Experience of supervising students is beneficial and it is expected that the post holder will work independently, taking a leading role in research in the lab. The post holder must be able to work to ISO9001 quality standards.

Good organisational and communication skills are essential, as the post holder will be working as part of a dynamic team, with a range of academic and industrial partners. Appropriate further training and personal professional development will be positively encouraged.
